sentences.zh: 自夫有天地焉，有人物焉，樹司牧以君臨，懸政教而成務，莫不擬乾坤之大象，稟中和以建極，揆影響之幽賾，成律呂之精微。

translations.literal: Since there have been Heaven and Earth, and since there have been people and things, in establishing rulers to govern and in setting forth government and teaching to accomplish their tasks, none have failed to take the great images of Heaven and Earth as their model, to receive the Mean and Harmony in establishing the supreme standard, to measure the hidden depths of shadow and influence, and to achieve the subtle refinements of pitch pipes and bell tones.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment Heaven and Earth existed and humanity arose, every ruler who governed and every state that taught its people modeled itself on the cosmos, drew on cosmic balance to set standards, read nature's hidden signs, and perfected the science of pitch and measure.

sentences.zh: 是用範圍百度，財成萬品。

translations.literal: By this means they encompassed the hundred measures and completed the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they regulated all standards and shaped the ten thousand kinds of things.

sentences.zh: 昔者淳古葦籥，創睹人籟之源，女媧笙簧，仍昭鳳律之首。

translations.literal: In antiquity, in the pure ancient age, reed pipes first revealed the source of human sounds; Nüwa's sheng and huang still proclaimed the beginning of the phoenix pitch.
translations.idiomatic: In deepest antiquity, reed flutes first disclosed the origin of human music; Nüwa's reed pipes still marked the first phoenix-toned pitch.

sentences.zh: 後聖廣業，稽古彌崇，伶倫含少，乃擅比竹之工，虞舜昭華，方傳刻玉之美。

translations.literal: Later sages expanded the enterprise and honored antiquity ever more highly: Ling Lun's Han Shao mastered the craft of comparing bamboo tubes; Shun of Yu with Zhao Hua transmitted the beauty of carving jade.
translations.idiomatic: Later sages enlarged the tradition and revered the past: Ling Lun's "Containing the Lesser" perfected the art of calibrated bamboo pipes; Yu Shun's Bright Splendor preserved the craft of jade pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 是以《書》稱：「葉時月正日，同律度量衡。

translations.literal: Therefore the Book of Documents says: "The seasons, the months, the corrected day, and the pitch pipes, measures, and weights are all in accord."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Documents states: "Align the seasons, months, and corrected day with unified pitch pipes, measures, and weights."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「予欲聞六律、五聲、八音、七始詠，以出納五言。

translations.literal: It also says: "I wish to hear the six pitch standards, the five notes, the eight timbres, and the seven beginnings chanted, so as to bring forth and receive the five words."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "I desire to hear the six pitch standards, five tones, eight timbres, and seven beginnings sung, to produce and receive the five-word verses."

sentences.zh: 」此皆候金常而列管，憑璿璣以運鈞，統三極之元，紀七衡之響，可以作樂崇德，殷薦上帝。

translations.literal: All these await the constant of metal to array the pipes, rely on the armillary sphere to turn the steelyard, unify the origin of the three ultimates, and record the resonance of the seven armillary rings—they can be used to make music and exalt virtue, and abundantly to offer to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: These all depend on metal bells to set the pipes, on the armillary instrument to drive the steelyard, to unify the three cosmic poles and mark the seven celestial harmonies—making music to ennoble virtue and richly offering worship to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故能動天地，感鬼神，和人心，移風俗，考得失，徵成敗者也。

translations.literal: Therefore they can move Heaven and Earth, touch spirits and ghosts, harmonize human hearts, transform customs, examine gain and loss, and verify success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Music thus moves Heaven and Earth, stirs spirits, harmonizes hearts, changes customs, and reveals success or failure.

sentences.zh: 粵在夏、商，無聞改作。

translations.literal: In Xia and Shang, nothing is recorded of changes or new creations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xia and Shang, no alterations to the system are recorded.

sentences.zh: 其于《周禮》，曲同則「掌六律六同之和，以辨天地四方陰陽之聲，以為樂器。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, in the section on pitch concordance, it states: "He manages the harmony of the six pitch standards and six concordances, to distinguish the sounds of Heaven and Earth, the four directions, yin and yang, and to make them into musical instruments."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou's section on pitch concordance says: "He oversees the harmony of the six pitch standards and six concordances, distinguishing the sounds of Heaven, Earth, the four directions, and yin and yang, for use in instruments."

sentences.zh: 」景王鑄鐘，問律於泠州鳩，對曰：「夫律者，所以立鈞出度。

translations.literal: When King Jing cast bells, he inquired about pitch from Leng Zhoujiu, who replied: "Pitch standards are what establish the steelyard and produce measures."
translations.idiomatic: When King Jing of Zhou cast bells, he asked Leng Zhoujiu about pitch; the reply was: "Pitch standards establish the steelyard and derive all measures."

sentences.zh: 」鈞有五，則權衡規矩準繩鹹備。

translations.literal: When the steelyard has five parts, then scales, steelyard-weights, compasses, squares, plumb lines, and measuring cords are all complete.
translations.idiomatic: With five parts to the steelyard, scales, weights, compasses, squares, plumb lines, and measuring cords all follow.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》曰：「尹氏太師，執國之鈞，天子是裨，俾眾不迷」是也。

translations.literal: Thus the Odes say: "The Grand Master Yin, holding the state's steelyard, assists the Son of Heaven and keeps the multitude from going astray"—this is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: As the Odes put it: "Grand Master Yin holds the nation's steelyard, assists the Son of Heaven, and keeps the people from losing their way."

sentences.zh: 太史公《律書》云：「王者制事立物，法度軌則，一稟於六律，為萬事之本。

translations.literal: Grand Historian Sima Qian's Treatise on Pitch Standards says: "The king, in establishing affairs and setting things in order, with laws, measures, and rules, takes the six pitch standards as the single source—the root of the ten thousand affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian's Treatise on Pitch Standards states: "The king, in ordering affairs and setting standards, derives all laws and measures from the six pitch standards—the foundation of everything."

sentences.zh: 其于兵械，尤所重焉。

translations.literal: In military weapons, they are especially valued.
translations.idiomatic: They are held in particular esteem for military equipment.

sentences.zh: 故云：'望敵知吉凶，聞聲效勝負。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "Gazing at the enemy reveals good or ill fortune; hearing sounds predicts victory or defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Look at the enemy and know fortune or misfortune; listen to sounds and foretell victory or defeat."

sentences.zh: 」百王不易之道也。

translations.literal: This is the Way that the hundred kings have never changed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the unchanging principle of all dynasties.

translations.literal: Close quotation mark.
translations.idiomatic: End of quotation.

sentences.zh: 及秦氏滅學，其道浸微。

translations.literal: When the Qin dynasty extinguished learning, this Way gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin suppressed scholarship, the tradition faded.

sentences.zh: 漢室初興，丞相張蒼，首言音律，未能審備。

translations.literal: When the Han house first rose, Chancellor Zhang Cang was the first to speak of pitch and pitch standards, but he could not examine and complete them fully.
translations.idiomatic: At Han's founding, Chancellor Zhang Cang first addressed pitch standards but could not complete a thorough review.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝創置協律之官，司馬遷言律呂相生之次詳矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han newly established the office of pitch-harmonizing official; Sima Qian's account of the order of mutual generation among pitch pipes and bell tones is detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu created the office of pitch harmonizer; Sima Qian gave a full account of how pitch pipes and bell tones generate one another.

sentences.zh: 及王莽之際，考論音律，劉歆條奏，班固因志之。

translations.literal: At the time of Wang Mang, pitch standards were examined and discussed; Liu Xin submitted a detailed memorial, and Ban Gu recorded it in his Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang, pitch standards were re-examined; Liu Xin submitted a detailed report, which Ban Gu incorporated into his Treatise.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕又記建武以後言律呂者，司馬紹統采而續之。

translations.literal: Cai Yong also recorded those who discussed pitch pipes and bell tones after the Jianwu era; Sima Shao continued and compiled their work.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong recorded post-Jianwu discussions of pitch and bell tones; Sima Shao collected and continued them.

sentences.zh: 炎曆將終，而天下大亂，樂工散亡，器法湮滅。

translations.literal: As the Han calendar neared its end, the realm fell into great disorder; music workers scattered and perished, and instruments and methods were lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Han neared collapse, the empire descended into chaos; musicians fled, and instruments and methods vanished.

sentences.zh: 魏武始獲杜夔，使定音律，夔依當時尺度，權備典章。

translations.literal: Cao Wu of Wei first obtained Du Kui and had him fix the pitch standards; Kui relied on the scales of the time and provisionally restored the canonical regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Cao Cao first acquired Du Kui and charged him with fixing pitch standards, using contemporary measures to restore the canonical system as best he could.

sentences.zh: 及晉武受命，遵而不革。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Jin received the Mandate, he followed this without change.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Emperor Wu kept the system unchanged.

sentences.zh: 至泰始十年，光祿大夫荀勖，奏造新度，更鑄律呂。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taishi, Palace Attendant Xun Xu memorialized to create new measures and recast the pitch pipes and bell tones.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 10, Palace Attendant Xun Xu proposed new standard measures and a recasting of the pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 元康中，勖子籓複嗣其事。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era, Xu's son Fan again succeeded to the task.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang, Xu's son Fan took up the work again.

sentences.zh: 未及成功，屬永嘉之亂，中朝典章，咸沒于石勒。

translations.literal: Before success was achieved, the Yongjia turmoil came; the canonical regulations of the central court were all lost to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Before the project finished, the Yongjia upheaval struck; the central court's standards were lost to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 及帝南遷，皇度草昧，禮容樂器，掃地皆盡。

translations.literal: When the emperor moved south, imperial institutions were still rudimentary; ritual forms and musical instruments were swept away entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After the court fled south, institutions were still primitive; ritual and musical equipment were utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 雖稍加采掇，而多所淪胥，終於恭、安，竟不能備。

translations.literal: Although some were gradually gathered again, many were lost; down to the Gong and An reigns, the system was never fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Some materials were recovered, but much was lost forever; through the Gong and An reigns, the system remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 宋錢樂之衍京房六十律，更增為三百六十，梁博士沈重，述其名數。

translations.literal: Song's Qian Yuezhi extended Jing Fang's sixty pitch standards to three hundred and sixty; Liang Academician Shen Chong set forth their names and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Qian Yuezhi expanded Jing Fang's sixty pitch standards to three hundred sixty; Liang scholar Shen Chong recorded their names and values.

sentences.zh: 後魏、周、齊，時有論者。

translations.literal: Later Wei, Zhou, and Qi each had their own theorists.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei, Northern Zhou, and Northern Qi all produced their own theorists.

sentences.zh: 今依班志，編錄五代聲律度量，以志於篇雲。

translations.literal: Now, following Ban's Treatise, the pitch standards, measures, and weights of five dynasties are compiled and recorded in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Following Ban Gu's Treatise, this chapter records the pitch standards, measures, and weights of five dynasties.

sentences.zh: 《漢志》言律，一曰備數，二曰和聲，三曰審度，四曰嘉量，五曰衡權。

translations.literal: The Han Treatise on pitch standards speaks of five aspects: first, complete numbers; second, harmonizing sounds; third, examining measures; fourth, commended capacity; fifth, steelyard and weights.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Treatise lists five aspects of pitch standards: complete numbers, harmonizing sounds, examining measures, commended capacity, and steelyard weights.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉已降，代有沿革。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, each age had its revisions and changes.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, each dynasty revised the system.

sentences.zh: 今列其增損之要雲。

translations.literal: Now the essentials of these additions and subtractions are listed below.
translations.idiomatic: The key changes are summarized here.

sentences.zh: 備數五數者，一、十、百、千、萬也。

translations.literal: Complete numbers: the five numbers are one, ten, hundred, thousand, and ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The five complete numbers are one, ten, hundred, thousand, and ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「物生而後有象，滋而後有數。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "After things arise, images appear; after they multiply, numbers appear."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary states: "Things first exist, then images form; as they proliferate, numbers emerge."

sentences.zh: 」是以言律者，雲數起於建子，黃鐘之律，始一，而每辰三之，曆九辰至酉，得一萬九千六百八十三，而五數備成，以為律法。

translations.literal: Therefore those who speak of pitch standards say that numbers begin from the jianzi month; the Yellow Bell pitch standard starts at one, and for each double-hour period it is multiplied by three; passing through nine periods to you, one obtains 19,683, and the five numbers are complete—this becomes the pitch-standard law.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch theorists hold that counting begins at the jianzi month: the Yellow Bell pitch starts at one, triples each two-hour period, and after nine periods reaches 19,683—completing the five numbers and forming the pitch law.

sentences.zh: 又參之，終亥，凡曆十二辰，得十有七萬七千一百四十七，而辰數該矣，以為律積。

translations.literal: Multiplying further through to hai, passing through all twelve double-hour periods in all, one obtains 177,147, and the double-hour numbers are complete—this becomes the pitch accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Continuing through all twelve periods to hai yields 177,147—the full period accumulation.

sentences.zh: 以成法除該積，得九寸，即黃鐘宮律之長也。

translations.literal: Dividing this accumulation by the completed law yields nine inches—the length of the Yellow Bell palace pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing that accumulation by the completed law gives nine inches—the length of the Yellow Bell palace pipe.

sentences.zh: 此則數因律起，律以數成，故可曆管萬事，綜核氣象。

translations.literal: Thus numbers arise from pitch standards, and pitch standards are completed by numbers; therefore they can govern the ten thousand affairs and comprehensively verify cosmic phenomena.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers derive from pitch, and pitch is fixed by numbers—so they can regulate all affairs and verify cosmic patterns.

sentences.zh: 其算用竹，廣二分，長三寸，正策三廉，積二百一十六枚，成六觚，乾之策也。

translations.literal: The counting rods are made of bamboo, two fen wide and three cun long; the positive rods have three edges, 216 pieces in all, forming a hexagonal prism—the Qian counting rods.
translations.idiomatic: Counting rods are bamboo strips two fen wide and three cun long; positive rods with three edges, 216 in all, form a hexagonal prism—the Qian rods.

sentences.zh: 負策四廉，積一百四十四枚，成方，坤之策也。

translations.literal: The negative rods have four edges, 144 pieces in all, forming a square—the Kun counting rods.
translations.idiomatic: Negative rods with four edges, 144 in all, form a square—the Kun rods.

sentences.zh: 觚方皆經十二，天地之大數也。

translations.literal: Both hexagon and square are measured by twelve—the great numbers of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Hexagon and square both use twelve as their measure—the great numbers of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 是故探賾索隱，鉤深致遠，莫不用焉。

translations.literal: Therefore in probing hidden depths, seeking what is concealed, reaching into the profound and extending to the distant, none fail to use them.
translations.idiomatic: In probing mysteries and reaching into the profound, nothing is done without them.

sentences.zh: 一、十、百、千、萬，所同由也。

translations.literal: One, ten, hundred, thousand, and ten thousand are what all share in common.
translations.idiomatic: One through ten thousand are the shared foundation.

sentences.zh: 律、度、量、衡、曆、率，其別用也。

translations.literal: Pitch standards, length measure, capacity measure, steelyard and weights, calendar, and proportional calculation are what differ in use.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch, length, capacity, weight, calendar, and proportional calculation are the separate applications.

sentences.zh: 故體有長短，檢之以度，則不失毫釐；

translations.literal: Therefore bodies have length and shortness; checking them with length measure, not a hair or tip of a awl is lost;
translations.idiomatic: Bodies vary in length; measured by the ruler, not a hair's breadth is missed;

sentences.zh: 物有多少，受之以器，則不失圭撮；

translations.literal: things have more or less; receiving them in vessels, not a grain or spoonful is lost;
translations.idiomatic: quantities vary in amount; held in vessels, not a grain or spoonful is lost;

sentences.zh: 量有輕重，平之以權衡，則不失黍絲；

translations.literal: weights have light and heavy; balancing them with steelyard and scales, not a millet seed or silk thread is lost;
translations.idiomatic: mass varies in weight; balanced on scales, not a millet seed or silk thread is missed;

sentences.zh: 聲有清濁，協之以律呂，則不失宮商；

translations.literal: sounds have clear and muddy; harmonizing them with pitch pipes and bell tones, not a note of gong or shang is lost;
translations.idiomatic: sounds vary in pitch; harmonized by pitch pipes, not a note of gong or shang is missed;

sentences.zh: 三光運行，紀以歷數，則不差晷刻；

translations.literal: the three luminaries move; recording them with calendrical numbers, not a gnomon mark or quarter-hour is missed;
translations.idiomatic: the sun, moon, and stars move; tracked by calendrical reckoning, not a moment is missed;

sentences.zh: 事物糅見，禦之以率，則不乖其本。

translations.literal: things mixed and appearing together are governed by proportional calculation, and their root is not violated.
translations.idiomatic: complex mixed quantities are handled by proportional calculation without losing their basis.

sentences.zh: 故幽隱之情，精微之變，可得而綜也。

translations.literal: Therefore hidden sentiments and subtle transformations can be comprehensively grasped.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden truths and subtle changes can thus be fully comprehended.

sentences.zh: 夫所謂率者，有九流焉：一曰方田，以禦田疇界域。

translations.literal: What are called proportional calculations comprise nine branches: first, rectangular fields, to govern field boundaries and areas.
translations.idiomatic: Proportional calculation has nine branches: first, rectangular fields, for land boundaries and areas.

sentences.zh: 二曰栗米，以禦交質變易。

translations.literal: Second, millet and rice, to govern exchange and conversion of commodities.
translations.idiomatic: Second, millet and rice, for commodity exchange and conversion.

sentences.zh: 三曰衰分，以禦貴賤廩稅。

translations.literal: Third, proportional distribution, to govern noble and base, granary levies and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Third, proportional distribution, for rank-based grain levies and taxes.

sentences.zh: 四曰少廣，以禦積冪方圓。

translations.literal: Fourth, lesser breadth, to govern volumes and areas of squares and circles.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, lesser breadth, for volumes and areas of squares and circles.

sentences.zh: 五曰商功，以禦功程積實。

translations.literal: Fifth, construction works, to govern labor projects, volumes, and solid quantities.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, construction works, for engineering projects and solid volumes.

sentences.zh: 六曰均輸，以禦遠近勞費。

translations.literal: Sixth, fair transportation, to govern labor and expense over near and far distances.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, fair transportation, for labor and cost over varying distances.

sentences.zh: 七曰盈肭，以禦隱雜互見。

translations.literal: Seventh, excess and deficit, to govern hidden and mixed quantities appearing together.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, excess and deficit, for hidden quantities appearing in mixed problems.

sentences.zh: 八曰方程，以禦錯糅正負。

translations.literal: Eighth, rectangular arrays, to govern tangled positive and negative quantities.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, rectangular arrays, for systems of positive and negative quantities.

sentences.zh: 九曰句股，以禦高深廣遠。

translations.literal: Ninth, right triangles and legs, to govern height, depth, breadth, and distance.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, right triangles and legs, for height, depth, width, and distance.

sentences.zh: 皆乘以散之，除以聚之，齊同以通之，今有以貫之。

translations.literal: All are multiplied to disperse, divided to gather, equalized and unified to connect, and the present quantity is used to thread them through.
translations.idiomatic: All are multiplied to expand, divided to consolidate, equalized to connect, and unified by the present quantity.

sentences.zh: 則算數之方，盡於斯矣。

translations.literal: Then the methods of calculation are fully exhausted in these.
translations.idiomatic: The full scope of calculation is contained in these.

sentences.zh: 古之九數，圓周率三，圓徑率一，其術疏舛。

translations.literal: In the ancient Nine Chapters, the ratio of circumference to diameter was three to one; the method was crude and erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient Nine Chapters used a circumference-to-diameter ratio of three to one—a crude approximation.

sentences.zh: 自劉歆、張衡、劉徽、王蕃、皮延宗之徒，各設新率，未臻折衷。

translations.literal: From Liu Xin, Zhang Heng, Liu Hui, Wang Fan, Pi Yanzong, and others, each set a new ratio, but none reached a balanced mean.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin, Zhang Heng, Liu Hui, Wang Fan, Pi Yanzong, and others each proposed new ratios, but none achieved a definitive value.

sentences.zh: 宋末，南徐州從事史祖沖之，更開密法，以圓徑一億為一丈，圓周盈數三丈一尺四寸一分五厘九毫二秒七忽，朒數三丈一尺四寸一分五厘九毫二秒六忽，正數在盈朒二限之間。

translations.literal: At the end of Song, Zu Chongzhi, Attendant Clerk of Southern Xuzhou, opened a more precise method: taking a diameter of one hundred million as one zhang, the excess circumference was three zhang one chi four cun one fen five li nine hao two miao seven hu, the deficit circumference was three zhang one chi four cun one fen five li nine hao two miao six hu, and the true value lay between the excess and deficit limits.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Song, Zu Chongzhi of Southern Xuzhou developed a precise method: with a diameter of one hundred million as one zhang, the excess circumference was 3.1415927 zhang and the deficit 3.1415926 zhang—the true value falling between.

sentences.zh: 密率，圓徑一百一十三，圓周三百五十五。

translations.literal: The precise ratio: diameter 113, circumference 355.
translations.idiomatic: Zu's precise ratio was 113 to 355 for diameter and circumference.

sentences.zh: 約率，圓徑七，週二十二。

translations.literal: The approximating ratio: diameter 7, circumference 22.
translations.idiomatic: His rough ratio was 7 to 22.

sentences.zh: 又設開差冪，開差立，兼以正圓參之。

translations.literal: He also devised methods for extracting roots of differences and powers, combining them with verification by regular circles.
translations.idiomatic: He also devised root extraction for differences and powers, cross-checked against regular circles.

sentences.zh: 指要精密，算氏之最者也。

translations.literal: The essentials are precise and subtle—the highest achievement of the calculators.
translations.idiomatic: His methods were precise and subtle—the finest achievement in mathematics.

sentences.zh: 所著之書，名為《綴術》，學官莫能究其深奧，是故廢而不理。

translations.literal: The book he wrote was called the Method of Interpolation; the academicians could not fathom its profundity, and so it was abandoned and left untended.
translations.idiomatic: His book, the Method of Interpolation, was too profound for the academicians to master, and it fell into neglect.

sentences.zh: ○和聲

translations.literal: ○ Harmonizing Sounds
translations.idiomatic: ○ On Harmonizing Sounds

sentences.zh: 傳稱黃帝命伶倫斷竹，長三寸九分，而吹以為黃鐘之宮，曰含少。

translations.literal: Tradition says the Yellow Emperor ordered Ling Lun to cut bamboo nine fen and three cun long and blow it to make the Yellow Bell palace pitch, called Han Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition holds that the Yellow Emperor ordered Ling Lun to cut a bamboo tube three cun nine fen long and blow it to produce the Yellow Bell palace pitch, called "Containing the Lesser."

sentences.zh: 次制十二管，以聽鳳鳴，以別十二律，此雌雄之聲，以分律呂。

translations.literal: Next he made twelve pipes to listen to the phoenix's cry, to distinguish the twelve pitch standards—this is the male and female sound, to divide pitch pipes and bell tones.
translations.idiomatic: He then made twelve pipes to listen for the phoenix's call, distinguishing the twelve pitch standards—the male and female tones that divide the pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 上下相生，因黃鐘為始。

translations.literal: Generating upward and downward, taking Yellow Bell as the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Upward and downward generation begins from Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 《虞書》云：「葉時月正日，同律度量衡。

translations.literal: The Book of Yu says: "The seasons, the months, the corrected day, and the pitch pipes, measures, and weights are all in accord."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Yu states: "Align the seasons, months, and corrected day with unified pitch pipes, measures, and weights."

sentences.zh: 」夏禹受命，以聲為律，以身為度。

translations.literal: When Xia Yu received the Mandate, he took sound as pitch standard and his body as measure.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu of Xia received the Mandate, he used sound for pitch and his body for measure.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》，樂器以十二律為之度數。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, musical instruments take the twelve pitch standards as their measures.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou specifies that instruments are sized by the twelve pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷《律書》云：「黃鐘長八寸七分之一，太簇長七寸七分二，林鐘長五寸七分三，應鐘長四寸三分二。

translations.literal: Sima Qian's Treatise on Pitch Standards says: "Yellow Bell is eight cun and one-seventh long; Great Cluster is seven cun and seven-sevenths and two; Forest Bell is five cun and seven-sevenths and three; Responding Bell is four cun and three-sevenths and two."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian's Treatise gives: Yellow Bell eight cun and one-seventh; Great Cluster seven cun and seven-sevenths and two; Forest Bell five cun and seven-sevenths and three; Responding Bell four cun and three-sevenths and two.

sentences.zh: 」此樂之三始，十二律之本末也。

translations.literal: These are the three beginnings of music and the root and branch of the twelve pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: These are the three origins of music and the foundation of the twelve pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 班固、司馬彪《律志》：「黃鐘長九寸，聲最濁；

translations.literal: Ban Gu and Sima Biao's Treatise on Pitch Standards: "Yellow Bell is nine cun long, the sound most muddy;"
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu and Sima Biao's Treatise: "Yellow Bell is nine cun long, the lowest pitch;"

sentences.zh: 太簇長八寸；

translations.literal: Great Cluster is eight cun long;
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster measures eight cun;

sentences.zh: 林鐘長六寸；

translations.literal: Forest Bell is six cun long;
translations.idiomatic: Forest Bell measures six cun;

sentences.zh: 應鐘長四寸七分四厘強，聲最清。

translations.literal: Responding Bell is four cun seven fen four li and a fraction strong, the sound most clear.
translations.idiomatic: Responding Bell is four cun seven fen four li and a fraction, the highest pitch.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄《禮·月令注》、蔡邕《月令章句》及杜夔、荀勖等所論，雖尺有增損，而十二律之寸數並同。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Monthly Ordinances in the Rites, Cai Yong's chapter on the Monthly Ordinances, and the discussions of Du Kui, Xun Xu, and others—although the foot measure had additions and subtractions, the cun numbers of the twelve pitch standards were all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan, Cai Yong, Du Kui, and Xun Xu debated the measures, but all agreed on the cun lengths of the twelve pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 《漢志》京房又以隔八相生，一始自黃鐘，終於中呂，十二律畢矣。

translations.literal: The Han Treatise: Jing Fang also used generation across eight pitch standards; beginning from Yellow Bell and ending at Middle Bell Female, the twelve pitch standards were complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Treatise adds: Jing Fang used generation across eight steps—from Yellow Bell through Middle Bell Female, completing the twelve standards.

sentences.zh: 中呂上生黃鐘，不滿九寸，謂之執始，下生去滅。

translations.literal: Middle Bell Female generates Yellow Bell upward, not reaching nine cun—this is called Holding the Beginning; generating downward removes the excess.
translations.idiomatic: Middle Bell Female generates Yellow Bell upward but falls short of nine cun—called "Holding the Beginning"; downward generation subtracts the remainder.

sentences.zh: 上下相生，終於南事，更增四十八律，以為六十。

translations.literal: Generating upward and downward, ending at Southern Affair, forty-eight pitch standards were added to make sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Upward and downward generation, ending at Southern Affair, added forty-eight standards to make sixty.

sentences.zh: 其依行在辰，上生包育，隔九編於冬至之後。

translations.literal: Those whose generating line falls in the chen period generate Bao Yu upward, spaced nine entries after the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Those generating from the chen period produce Bao Yu upward, nine steps after the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 分焉、遲內，其數遂減應鐘之清。

translations.literal: Fen Yan and Chi Nei—their numbers then reduce the clarity of Responding Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Fen Yan and Chi Nei reduce the clarity of Responding Bell.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，太史錢樂之因京房南事之餘，引而伸之，更為三百律，終於安運，長四寸四分有奇。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Liu Song, Grand Astrologer Qian Yuezhi, following the remainder of Jing Fang's Southern Affair, extended it further to three hundred pitch standards, ending at An Yun, four cun four fen and a fraction long.
translations.idiomatic: In Liu Song's Yuanjia era, Grand Astrologer Qian Yuezhi extended Jing Fang's Southern Affair to three hundred pitch standards, ending at An Yun at four cun four fen and a fraction.

sentences.zh: 總合舊為三百六十律。

translations.literal: In total, combined with the old, there were three hundred and sixty pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Combined with the earlier standards, the total reached three hundred sixty pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 日當一管，宮徵旋韻，各以次從。

translations.literal: Each day corresponded to one pipe; palace and zhi modes rotated in sequence, each following in order.
translations.idiomatic: One pipe per day; palace and zhi modes cycled in sequence.

sentences.zh: 何承天《立法制議》云：「上下相生，三分損益其一，蓋是古人簡易之法。

translations.literal: He Chengtian's "Discourse on Establishing Laws and Systems" says: "Generating upward and downward, taking one-third and adding or subtracting one—this is the ancients' simple method."
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's Discourse on Establishing Laws states: "Upward and downward generation by adding or subtracting one-third was the ancients' simple method."

sentences.zh: 猶如古曆周天三百六十五度四分之一，後人改制，皆不同焉。

translations.literal: It is like the ancient calendar's circuit of heaven of 365 and one-quarter degrees; later people reformed the system, and all differed.
translations.idiomatic: Like the ancient calendar's 365¼-day year—later reformers all produced different values.

sentences.zh: 而京房不悟，謬為六十。

translations.literal: But Jing Fang did not understand this and erroneously made sixty pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang failed to grasp this and wrongly devised sixty pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 」承天更設新率，則從中呂還得黃鐘，十二旋宮，聲韻無失。

translations.literal: He Chengtian, setting a new ratio in accord with Heaven, then from Middle Bell Female returns to Yellow Bell; the twelve rotating palaces—sound and pitch are without loss.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's new ratio returns from Middle Bell Female to Yellow Bell; the twelve rotating modes preserve pitch without error.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘長九寸，太簇長八寸二厘，林鐘長六寸一厘，應鐘長四寸七分九厘強。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell is nine cun long; Great Cluster is eight cun two li; Forest Bell is six cun one li; Responding Bell is four cun seven fen nine li and a fraction strong.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell nine cun; Great Cluster eight cun two li; Forest Bell six cun one li; Responding Bell four cun seven fen nine li and a fraction.

sentences.zh: 其中呂上生所益之分，還得十七萬七千一百四十七，複十二辰參之數。

translations.literal: The portion added by Middle Bell Female's upward generation again yields 177,147—the number multiplied through the twelve double-hour periods.
translations.idiomatic: The increment from Middle Bell Female's upward generation again yields 177,147—the full twelve-period product.

sentences.zh: 梁初，因晉、宋及齊，無所改制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang, following Jin, Song, and Qi, no reforms were made.
translations.idiomatic: Early Liang retained the systems of Jin, Song, and Qi without change.

sentences.zh: 其後武帝作《鐘律緯》，論前代得失。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Wu wrote the Treatise on Bell Standards and Pitch Pipes, discussing the gains and losses of previous ages.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wu of Liang wrote the Treatise on Bell Standards and Pitch Pipes, reviewing earlier successes and failures.

sentences.zh: 其略云：

translations.literal: The summary says:
translations.idiomatic: In summary:

sentences.zh: 案律呂，京、馬、鄭、蔡，至蕤賓，並上生大呂；

translations.literal: Examining pitch pipes and bell tones: Jing Fang, Ma Rong, Zheng Xuan, and Cai Yong, up to Luxuriant Guest, all generate Great Bell upward;
translations.idiomatic: On pitch pipes: Jing Fang, Ma Rong, Zheng Xuan, and Cai Yong all generate Great Bell upward through Luxuriant Guest;

sentences.zh: 而班固《律曆志》，至蕤賓，仍以次下生。

translations.literal: But Ban Gu's Treatise on Pitch Standards and the Calendar, up to Luxuriant Guest, still generates downward in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's Treatise, however, generates downward in sequence through Luxuriant Guest.

sentences.zh: 若從班義，夾鐘唯長三寸七分有奇。

translations.literal: If one follows Ban's meaning, Pinched Bell would be only three cun seven fen and a fraction long.
translations.idiomatic: Following Ban's view, Pinched Bell would measure only three cun seven fen and a fraction.

sentences.zh: 律若過促，則夾鐘之聲成一調，中呂複去調半，是過於無調。

translations.literal: If the pitch standard is too short, then Pinched Bell's sound becomes a single mode, and Middle Bell Female again loses half a mode—this is excessive lack of mode.
translations.idiomatic: Overly short pipes make Pinched Bell a single mode and Middle Bell Female lose half a mode—leaving the system without proper tuning.

sentences.zh: 仲春孟夏，正相長養，其氣舒緩，不容短促。

translations.literal: Mid-spring and early summer are precisely when growth and nourishment proceed; the qi is relaxed and slow—it cannot tolerate shortness and urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring and early summer nurture growth; the qi flows gently and cannot be compressed into overly short pipes.

sentences.zh: 求聲索實，班義為乖。

translations.literal: Seeking sound and verifying reality, Ban's meaning is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against acoustic reality, Ban's interpretation fails.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄又以陰陽六位，次第相生。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan also used the six positions of yin and yang, generating in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also arranged generation by the six yin-yang positions in sequence.

sentences.zh: 若如玄義，陰陽相逐生者，止是升陽，其降陽複將何寄？

translations.literal: If one follows Xuan's meaning, yin and yang generating in mutual pursuit—only ascending yang is accounted for; where then is descending yang placed?
translations.idiomatic: On Zheng's view, mutual yin-yang generation accounts only for ascending yang—leaving nowhere for descending yang.

sentences.zh: 就筮數而論，乾主甲壬而左行，坤主乙癸而右行，故陰陽得有升降之義。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of divination numbers: Qian governs jia and ren and moves left; Kun governs yi and gui and moves right—therefore yin and yang can have the meaning of ascent and descent.
translations.idiomatic: In divination terms, Qian governs jia and ren moving left, Kun governs yi and gui moving right—giving yin and yang their ascending and descending roles.

sentences.zh: 陰陽從行者，真性也，六位升降者，象數也。

translations.literal: Yin and yang following in movement is true nature; the six positions ascending and descending is symbolic number.
translations.idiomatic: Yin-yang in motion is true nature; the six positions rising and falling are symbolic numbers.

sentences.zh: 今鄭乃執象數以配真性，故言比而理窮。

translations.literal: Now Zheng holds symbolic number to match true nature; therefore his words compare but reason is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng forced symbolic numbers onto true nature—his analogy collapses under scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 雲九六相生，了不釋十二氣所以相通，鄭之不思，亦已明矣。

translations.literal: Speaking of nine and six generating each other, he entirely fails to explain why the twelve qi connect; Zheng's failure to think is already clear.
translations.idiomatic: His talk of nine and six generating each other never explains how the twelve qi connect—Zheng simply did not think it through.

sentences.zh: 案京房六十，准依法推，乃自無差。

translations.literal: Examining Jing Fang's sixty pitch standards, pushing by the proper law, there is naturally no discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's sixty standards, properly calculated, are internally consistent.

sentences.zh: 但律呂所得，或五或六，此一不例也。

translations.literal: But the pitch pipes and bell tones obtained are sometimes five, sometimes six—this is the first irregularity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the resulting pitch values are sometimes five, sometimes six—the first irregularity.

sentences.zh: 而分焉上生，乃複遲內上生盛變，盛變仍複上生分居，此二不例也。

translations.literal: Yet Fen Yan generates upward, then again Chi Nei generates Sheng Bian upward, and Sheng Bian again generates Fen Ju upward—this is the second irregularity.
translations.idiomatic: Fen Yan generates upward, then Chi Nei generates Sheng Bian, which generates Fen Ju—this is the second irregularity.

sentences.zh: 房妙盡陰陽，其當有以，若非深理難求，便是傳者不習。

translations.literal: Fang exhaustively mastered yin and yang; there must be a reason for this—if it is not that the deep principle is hard to seek, then the transmitters did not understand the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Fang mastered yin-yang theory; either the deep principle is elusive or later transmitters did not understand his method.

sentences.zh: 比敕詳求，莫能辨正。

translations.literal: An edict ordered detailed investigation, but none could distinguish and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order demanded clarification, but no one could resolve the discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 聊以餘日，試推其旨，參校舊器，及古夾鐘玉律，更制新尺，以證分毫，制為四器，名之為通。

translations.literal: For the moment, in spare time, I tried to deduce its intent, compared old instruments and the ancient Pinched Bell jade pitch standard, and made a new foot measure to verify fen and hao, making four instruments called the Tong.
translations.idiomatic: In spare time I deduced the theory, compared old instruments with the ancient Pinched Bell jade pipe, made a new ruler to verify measurements, and created four instruments called the Tong.

sentences.zh: 四器弦間九尺，臨岳高一寸二分。

translations.literal: The four instruments have nine chi between the strings; the bridge height is one cun two fen.
translations.idiomatic: The four instruments span nine chi between strings, with bridge height of one cun two fen.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之弦二百七十絲，長九尺，以次三分損益其一，以生十二律之弦絲數及弦長。

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell string has 270 silk threads, nine chi long; by adding or subtracting one-third in sequence, the silk thread counts and string lengths of the twelve pitch standards are generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell string uses 270 silk threads nine chi long; tripling or dividing by three in sequence yields the twelve pitch strings.

sentences.zh: 各以律本所建之月，五行生王，終始之音，相次之理，為其名義，名之為通。

translations.literal: Each takes the month established by the pitch root, the waxing and waning of the five phases, the beginning and ending notes, and the principle of successive order as its name and meaning—called the Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Each was named by the month of its pitch root, the five phases' waxing and waning, and the logic of successive tones—the Tong instruments.

sentences.zh: 通施三弦，傳推月氣，悉無差舛。

translations.literal: The Tong applied to three strings; transmitting and deducing monthly qi, all were without error.
translations.idiomatic: Applied to three strings, the monthly qi calculations matched without error.

sentences.zh: 即以夾鐘玉律命之，則還相中。

translations.literal: Taking the Pinched Bell jade pitch standard to tune them, they matched each other.
translations.idiomatic: Tuned against the Pinched Bell jade pipe, they matched perfectly.

sentences.zh: 又制為十二笛，以寫通聲。

translations.literal: Twelve flutes were also made to reproduce the Tong sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve flutes were also made to replicate the Tong sounds.

sentences.zh: 其夾鐘笛十二調，以飲玉律，又不差異。

translations.literal: The Pinched Bell flute's twelve modes, tested against the jade pitch standard, showed no discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: The Pinched Bell flute's twelve modes matched the jade pitch standard without deviation.

sentences.zh: 山謙之《記》云：「殿前三鐘，悉是周景王所鑄無射也。

translations.literal: Shan Qianzhi's Record says: "The three bells before the hall are all the Pitchless cast by King Jing of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Shan Qianzhi's Record states: "The three hall bells are all Pitchless bells cast by King Jing of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」遣樂官以今無射新笛飲，不相中。

translations.literal: Musicians were sent to test with the new Pitchless flute of today—they did not match.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians tested them with the current Pitchless flute—they did not match.

sentences.zh: 以夷則笛飲，則聲韻合和。

translations.literal: Testing with the Luxuriant Guest flute, sound and pitch harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: With the Luxuriant Guest flute, the tones harmonized.

sentences.zh: 端門外鐘，亦案其銘題，定皆夷則。

translations.literal: The bell outside the Duan Gate—examining its inscription, it is fixed as Luxuriant Guest.
translations.idiomatic: The bell outside the Duan Gate, its inscription confirms it as Luxuriant Guest.

sentences.zh: 其西廂一鐘，天監中移度東。

translations.literal: One bell in the west wing—in the Tianjian era was moved to the east.
translations.idiomatic: One west-wing bell was moved east in the Tianjian era.

sentences.zh: 以今笛飲，乃中南呂。

translations.literal: Testing with today's flute, it matched Southern Bell Female.
translations.idiomatic: Tested with the current flute, it matched Southern Bell Female.

sentences.zh: 驗其鐫刻，乃是太簇，則下今笛二調。

translations.literal: Verifying its inscription, it is actually Great Cluster—two modes below today's flute.
translations.idiomatic: Its inscription reads Great Cluster—two modes lower than the current flute.

sentences.zh: 重敕太樂丞斯宣達，令更推校，鐘定有鑿處，表裡皆然。

translations.literal: An edict was sent to Grand Music Director Si Xuanda ordering further verification; the bell's fixed point had chisel marks, the same inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Si Xuanda was ordered to re-examine the bell; chisel marks at the tuning point appeared on both sides.

sentences.zh: 借訪舊識，乃是宋泰始中，使張永鑿之，去銅既多，故其調嘽下。

translations.literal: Consulting old acquaintances, it was in Song's Taishi era that Zhang Yong was sent to chisel it; much copper was removed, and therefore its pitch was too low.
translations.idiomatic: Old records show Zhang Yong chiseled it in Song's Taishi era, removing so much copper that its pitch dropped.

sentences.zh: 以推求鐘律，便可得而見也。

translations.literal: From this, investigating bell standards and pitch pipes, the truth can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Thus investigating bell and pitch standards reveals the truth.

sentences.zh: 宋武平中原，使將軍陳傾致三鐘，小大中各一。

translations.literal: When Song Wu pacified the Central Plains, he sent General Chen Qing to deliver three bells—small, medium, and large, one each.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Song's Emperor Wu pacified the north, General Chen Qing delivered three bells—small, medium, and large.

sentences.zh: 則今之太極殿前二鐘，端門外一鐘是也。

translations.literal: These are the two bells before today's Hall of Supreme Ultimate and the one bell outside the Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: These are the two Supreme Ultimate Hall bells and the Duan Gate bell of today.

sentences.zh: 案西鐘銘則雲「清廟撞鐘」，秦無清廟，此周制明矣。

translations.literal: Examining the west bell's inscription, it says "Pure Temple Strike Bell"; Qin had no Pure Temple—this is clearly Zhou practice.
translations.idiomatic: The west bell's inscription reads "Pure Temple Strike Bell"; Qin had no Pure Temple—clearly a Zhou bell.

sentences.zh: 又一銘雲「太簇鐘徵」，則林鐘宮所施也。

translations.literal: Another inscription says "Great Cluster Bell Zhi"—this is what Forest Bell palace uses.
translations.idiomatic: Another reads "Great Cluster Bell Zhi"—used in Forest Bell palace mode.

sentences.zh: 京房推用，似有由也。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's deductions in use seem to have a basis.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's method appears to have sound reasoning.

sentences.zh: 檢題既無秦、漢年代，直雲夷則、太簇，則非秦、漢明矣。

translations.literal: Examining the inscriptions, with no Qin or Han date, only saying Luxuriant Guest and Great Cluster—they are clearly not Qin or Han.
translations.idiomatic: The inscriptions bear no Qin or Han dates, only Luxuriant Guest and Great Cluster—not Qin or Han work.

sentences.zh: 古人性質，故作僮僕字，則題而言，彌驗非近。

translations.literal: People of antiquity by nature made servant-boy characters in inscriptions; speaking from the inscriptions, this further verifies they are not recent.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient craftsmen used servant-boy script in inscriptions—confirming these are not recent pieces.

sentences.zh: 且夫驗聲改政，則五音六律，非可差舛。

translations.literal: Moreover, verifying sound to reform government—the five notes and six pitch standards cannot differ and err.
translations.idiomatic: Sound must be verified to govern properly—the five notes and six standards cannot be mistaken.

sentences.zh: 工守其音，儒執其文，歷年永久，隔而不通。

translations.literal: Craftsmen guard the sounds; Confucians hold the texts—over years and ages, separated and not communicating.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen preserved the sounds while scholars held the texts—over centuries they lost contact.

sentences.zh: 無論樂奏，求之多缺，假使具存，亦不可用。

translations.literal: Not to mention musical performance—much is missing in inquiry; even if fully preserved, it still could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Musical performance itself is largely lost; even if texts survived intact, they could not be applied.

sentences.zh: 周頌漢歌，各敘功德，豈容複施後王，以濫名實？

translations.literal: Zhou hymns and Han songs each narrate merit and virtue—how could they be applied again to later kings, corrupting names and reality?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou hymns and Han songs celebrate specific achievements—how could they be reused for later rulers?

sentences.zh: 今率詳論，以言所見，並詔百司，以求厥中。

translations.literal: Now, following detailed discussion, I state what I have seen, and also edict the hundred offices to seek the balanced mean.
translations.idiomatic: I now present my findings and order the hundred offices to seek the balanced standard.

sentences.zh: 未及改制，遇侯景亂。

translations.literal: Before reform could be completed, the Hou Jing rebellion came.
translations.idiomatic: Reform was interrupted by the Hou Jing rebellion.

sentences.zh: 陳氏制度，亦無改作。

translations.literal: Chen's institutions also had no reforms.
translations.idiomatic: Chen made no reforms either.

sentences.zh: 西魏廢帝元年，周文攝政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Western Wei's Deposed Emperor, Zhou Wen held regency.
translations.idiomatic: In Western Wei's first year of the Deposed Emperor, Yuwen Tai held regency.

sentences.zh: 又詔尚書蘇綽詳正音律。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered Minister of Works Su Chuo to examine and correct pitch and pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Minister Su Chuo to examine and correct pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 綽時得宋尺，以定諸管，草創未就會閔帝受禪，政由塚宰，方有齊寇，事竟不行。

translations.literal: Chuo at the time obtained a Song foot measure to fix all pipes; the draft was not completed when Emperor Min received the Mandate; government was held by the regent; there was Qi invasion—the matter ultimately did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo obtained a Song foot measure to calibrate the pipes, but the project was unfinished when Emperor Min ascended; with Qi invading, the work never proceeded.

sentences.zh: 後掘太倉，得古玉鬥，按以造律及衡，其事又多湮沒。

translations.literal: Later, excavating the Grand Granary, an ancient jade dipper was found; using it to make pitch standards and steelyard weights, much of the matter was again lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later an ancient jade dipper was found in the Grand Granary; used to make pitch pipes and weights, but much was again lost.

sentences.zh: 至開皇初，詔太常牛弘議定律呂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, an edict ordered Grand Master of Ceremonies Niu Hong to discuss fixing pitch pipes and bell tones.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaihuang's opening, Grand Master Niu Hong was ordered to fix pitch and bell standards.

sentences.zh: 於是博征學者，序論其法，又未能決。

translations.literal: Thereupon scholars were broadly summoned to set forth and discuss the method, but again no decision could be reached.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars were summoned to debate the method, but no consensus emerged.

sentences.zh: 遇平江右，得陳氏律管十有二枚，並以付弘。

translations.literal: When the Jiang region was pacified, twelve Chen pitch pipes were obtained and all given to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the south, twelve Chen pitch pipes were delivered to Niu Hong.

sentences.zh: 遣曉音律者陳山陽太守毛爽及太樂令蔡子元、於普明等，以候節氣，作《律譜》。

translations.literal: Those skilled in pitch were sent—Chen, Governor of Shanyang Mao Shuang, and Grand Music Director Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and others—to observe seasonal nodes and compose the Treatise on Pitch Standards.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch experts including Mao Shuang of Shanyang and Grand Music Director Cai Ziyuan were sent to observe seasonal nodes and write the Treatise on Pitch Standards.

sentences.zh: 時爽年老，以白衣見高祖，授淮州刺史，辭不赴官。

translations.literal: At the time Shuang was old; he was received by the High Ancestor as a commoner and offered the post of Governor of Huai Province; he declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Shuang, though elderly, was received by Emperor Wen as a commoner and offered Huai Province; he declined.

sentences.zh: 因遣協律郎祖孝孫就其受法。

translations.literal: Therefore Pitch-Harmonizing Official Zu Xiaosun was sent to him to receive the method.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch-Harmonizing Official Zu Xiaosun was sent to learn the method from him.

sentences.zh: 弘又取此管，吹而定聲。

translations.literal: Hong also took these pipes and blew them to fix the sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong also used these pipes to establish the pitch.

sentences.zh: 既天下一統，異代器物，皆集樂府，曉音律者，頗議考核，以定鐘律。

translations.literal: Once the realm was unified, objects of different ages all gathered in the Music Office; those skilled in pitch largely debated and examined to fix bell and pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: With unification, instruments from all eras gathered at the Music Office; pitch experts debated to fix bell and pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 更造樂器，以被《皇夏》十四曲，高祖與朝賢聽之，曰：「此聲滔滔和雅，令人舒緩。

translations.literal: New instruments were made to accompany the fourteen movements of "August Sovereign"; the High Ancestor listened with court worthies and said: "This sound is flowing and harmonious, making one relaxed and at ease."
translations.idiomatic: New instruments accompanied the fourteen "August Sovereign" movements; Emperor Wen listened with his court and said: "This music flows harmoniously and puts one at ease."
End of quotation.

sentences.zh: 然萬物人事，非五行不生，非五行不成，非五行不滅。

translations.literal: Yet the ten thousand things and human affairs—without the five phases they are not born, without the five phases they are not completed, without the five phases they are not extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: All things and human affairs depend on the five phases for birth, completion, and extinction.

sentences.zh: 故五音用火尺，其事火重。

translations.literal: Therefore the five notes use the fire foot measure; fire is the weighty matter.
translations.idiomatic: The five notes therefore use the fire foot measure—fire being the dominant element.

sentences.zh: 用金尺則兵，用木尺則喪，用土尺則亂，用水尺則律呂合調，天下和平。

translations.literal: Using the metal foot measure brings warfare; using the wood foot measure brings mourning; using the earth foot measure brings disorder; using the water foot measure brings pitch pipes and bell tones in harmony and peace under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The metal measure brings war, wood brings mourning, earth brings disorder—but the water measure harmonizes pitch and brings peace.

sentences.zh: 魏及周、齊，貪布帛長度，故用土尺。

translations.literal: Wei and Zhou and Qi, coveting the length of cloth and silk, therefore used the earth foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Zhou, and Qi, seeking longer cloth measures, used the earth foot measure.

sentences.zh: 今此樂聲，是用水尺。

translations.literal: Now this musical sound uses the water foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: The current music uses the water foot measure.

sentences.zh: 江東尺短於土，長於水。

translations.literal: The Jiangdong foot measure is shorter than earth and longer than water.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangdong measure is shorter than the earth measure but longer than the water measure.

sentences.zh: 俗間不知者，見玉作，名為玉尺，見鐵作，名為鐵尺。

translations.literal: Those among the common people who do not know, seeing jade work call it the jade foot measure, seeing iron work call it the iron foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Common people, seeing jade instruments call them jade measures, seeing iron ones call them iron measures.

sentences.zh: 詔施用水尺律樂，其前代金石，並鑄毀之，以息物議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the use of water foot measure pitch music; the metal and stone of previous ages were all recast and destroyed, to quiet objectors' debate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mandated water-measure pitch music; older metal and stone instruments were recast to silence debate.

sentences.zh: 至仁壽四年，劉焯上啟於東宮，論張胄玄曆，兼論律呂。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Renshou, Liu Zhuo submitted a memorial to the Eastern Palace, discussing Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar and also discussing pitch pipes and bell tones.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou 4, Liu Zhuo memorialized the crown prince on Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar and pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 其大旨曰：「樂主於音，音定於律，音不以律，不可克諧，度律均鐘，於是乎在。

translations.literal: The main point says: "Music is governed by notes; notes are fixed by pitch standards; without pitch standards, notes cannot be harmonized; balancing pitch standards and bell tones lies herein."
translations.idiomatic: His main argument: "Music depends on notes, notes on pitch standards—without standards, harmony is impossible; balancing standards and bells is essential."

sentences.zh: 但律終小呂，數複黃鐘，舊計未精，終不復始。

translations.literal: But pitch standards end at Lesser Bell and the number returns to Yellow Bell; the old calculation was not precise and never returns to the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Standards end at Lesser Bell and return to Yellow Bell, but old calculations were imprecise and never truly cycled back.

sentences.zh: 故漢代京房，妄為六十，而宋代錢樂之更為三百六十。

translations.literal: Therefore Han's Jing Fang arbitrarily made sixty, and Song's Qian Yuezhi further made three hundred and sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Han's Jing Fang arbitrarily devised sixty standards, and Song's Qian Yuezhi three hundred sixty.

sentences.zh: 考禮詮次，豈有得然，化未移風，將恐由此。

translations.literal: Examining ritual order—how can this be acceptable? If custom does not shift with the wind, I fear it will be because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Examined against ritual order, this is untenable—and customs may suffer accordingly.

sentences.zh: 匪直長短失於其差，亦自管圍乖於其數。

translations.literal: Not only are length and shortness wrong in their discrepancy—the bore circumference also deviates in its number.
translations.idiomatic: Not only are lengths wrong—the pipe bore circumferences are also incorrect.

sentences.zh: 又尺寸意定，莫能詳考，既亂管弦，亦舛度量。

translations.literal: Also, the intended fixed dimensions cannot be examined in detail; both strings and pipes are confused, and measures and quantities are also wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The intended dimensions cannot be verified in detail; strings, pipes, and all measures are confused.

sentences.zh: 焯皆校定，庶有明發。

translations.literal: Zhuo all corrected and fixed them, hoping for clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhuo corrected all of these, seeking clarity.

sentences.zh: 」其黃鐘管六十三為實，以次每律減三分，以七為寸法。

translations.literal: His Yellow Bell pipe has 63 as the solid value; for each pitch standard in sequence, subtract three parts; using seven as the cun method.
translations.idiomatic: His Yellow Bell pipe used 63 as the base; each subsequent standard subtracted three parts, with seven as the cun divisor.

sentences.zh: 約之，得黃鐘長九寸，太簇長八寸一分四厘，林鐘長六寸，應鐘長四寸二分八厘七分之四。

translations.literal: Reducing: Yellow Bell is nine cun long; Great Cluster eight cun one fen four li; Forest Bell six cun; Responding Bell four cun two fen eight li seven-fourths.
translations.idiomatic: This yielded Yellow Bell nine cun, Great Cluster eight cun one fen four li, Forest Bell six cun, Responding Bell four cun two fen eight li and seven-fourths.

sentences.zh: 其年，高祖崩，煬帝初登，未遑改作，事遂寢廢。

translations.literal: That year the High Ancestor died; when Emperor Yang first ascended, there was no leisure for reform—the matter was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Wen died; Emperor Yang had no time for reform and the project lapsed.

sentences.zh: 其書亦亡。

translations.literal: His book is also lost.
translations.idiomatic: His treatise was lost as well.

sentences.zh: 大業二年，乃詔改用梁表律調鐘磬八音之器，比之前代，最為合古。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daye, an edict ordered changing to use Liang's external pitch standard to tune bells, chime stones, and the eight timbres—in comparison with previous ages, this was most in accord with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Daye 2 ordered adoption of Liang's external pitch standard for bells, chimes, and the eight timbres—the most antiquity-conforming system yet.

sentences.zh: 其制度文議，並毛爽舊律，並在江都淪喪。

translations.literal: The institutional documents and discussions, together with Mao Shuang's old pitch standards, were all lost at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The institutional records and Mao Shuang's old standards were all lost at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: ○律管圍容黍

translations.literal: ○ Bore Circumference and Millet Capacity of Pitch Pipes
translations.idiomatic: ○ On Pipe Bore Circumference and Millet Capacity

sentences.zh: 《漢志》云：「黃鐘圍九分，林鐘圍六分，太簇圍八分。

translations.literal: The Han Treatise says: "Yellow Bell circumference nine fen; Forest Bell circumference six fen; Great Cluster circumference eight fen."
translations.idiomatic: The Han Treatise gives: Yellow Bell bore nine fen, Forest Bell six fen, Great Cluster eight fen.

sentences.zh: 」《續志》及鄭玄並云：「十二律空，皆徑三分，圍九分。

translations.literal: The Continuation Treatise and Zheng Xuan both say: "The twelve pitch standard bores all have diameter three fen, circumference nine fen."
translations.idiomatic: The Continuation Treatise and Zheng Xuan both state: all twelve pipes have diameter three fen, circumference nine fen.

sentences.zh: 」後魏安豐王依班固《志》，林鐘空圍六分，及太簇空圍八分，作律吹之，不合黃鐘商徵之聲。

translations.literal: Northern Wei's Prince of Anfeng, following Ban Gu's Treatise, made Forest Bell bore circumference six fen and Great Cluster bore circumference eight fen; blowing them as pitch standards, they did not match Yellow Bell's shang and zhi sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei's Prince of Anfeng, following Ban Gu, made Forest Bell six fen and Great Cluster eight fen bore—but they failed to produce Yellow Bell's shang and zhi tones.

sentences.zh: 皆空圍九分，乃與均鐘器合。

translations.literal: All with bore circumference nine fen then matched the balanced bell instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Only nine-fen bore circumferences matched the balanced bell instrument.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年平陳後，牛弘、辛彥之、鄭譯、何妥等，參考古律度，各依時代，制其黃鐘之管，俱徑三分，長九寸。

translations.literal: After pacifying Chen in the ninth year of Kaihuang, Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, Zheng Yi, He Tuo, and others, consulting ancient pitch standard measures of each era, made Yellow Bell pipes—all diameter three fen, length nine cun.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Chen in Kaihuang 9, Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, Zheng Yi, and He Tuo made Yellow Bell pipes of each era—all three fen diameter, nine cun long.

sentences.zh: 度有損益，故聲有高下；

translations.literal: The measure had additions and subtractions, therefore sounds had high and low;
translations.idiomatic: Measure variations produced pitch differences;

sentences.zh: 圓徑長短，與度而差，故容黍不同。

translations.literal: circumference, diameter, length, and shortness differ with the measure, therefore millet capacity differs.
translations.idiomatic: bore size and length varied with the measure, so millet capacity differed.

sentences.zh: 今列其數雲。

translations.literal: Now their numbers are listed below.
translations.idiomatic: Their values are listed below.

sentences.zh: 晉前尺黃鐘容黍八百八粒。

translations.literal: The pre-Jin foot measure: Yellow Bell holds 808 millet grains.
translations.idiomatic: Pre-Jin measure: Yellow Bell bore held 808 millet grains.

sentences.zh: 梁法尺黃鐘容八百二十八。

translations.literal: The Liang legal foot measure: Yellow Bell holds 828.
translations.idiomatic: Liang legal measure: Yellow Bell held 828 grains.

sentences.zh: 梁表尺黃鐘三：其一容九百二十五，其一容九百一十，其一容一千一百二十。

translations.literal: The Liang shadow-table foot measure Yellow Bell has three: one holds 925, one holds 910, one holds 1,120.
translations.idiomatic: Liang shadow-table measure had three Yellow Bell pipes: holding 925, 910, and 1,120 grains respectively.

sentences.zh: 漢官尺黃鐘容九百三十九。

translations.literal: The Han official foot measure: Yellow Bell holds 939.
translations.idiomatic: Han official measure: Yellow Bell held 939 grains.

sentences.zh: 古銀錯題黃鐘籥容一千二百。

translations.literal: Ancient silver-inscribed Yellow Bell key holds 1,200.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient silver-inscribed Yellow Bell key held 1,200 grains.

sentences.zh: 宋氏尺，即鐵尺，黃鐘凡二：其一容一千二百，其一容一千四十七。

translations.literal: The Song foot measure, which is the iron foot measure—Yellow Bell has two: one holds 1,200, one holds 1,047.
translations.idiomatic: Song iron measure had two Yellow Bell pipes: one holding 1,200, one 1,047 grains.

sentences.zh: 後魏前尺黃鐘容一千一百一十五。

translations.literal: Northern Wei's early foot measure: Yellow Bell holds 1,115.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei early measure: Yellow Bell held 1,115 grains.

sentences.zh: 後周玉尺黃鐘容一千二百六十七。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou jade foot measure: Yellow Bell holds 1,267.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou jade measure: Yellow Bell held 1,267 grains.

sentences.zh: 後魏中尺黃鐘容一千五百五十五。

translations.literal: Northern Wei middle foot measure: Yellow Bell holds 1,555.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei middle measure: Yellow Bell held 1,555 grains.

sentences.zh: 後魏後尺黃鐘容一千八百一十九。

translations.literal: Northern Wei later foot measure: Yellow Bell holds 1,819.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei later measure: Yellow Bell held 1,819 grains.

sentences.zh: 東魏尺黃鐘容二千八百六十九。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei foot measure: Yellow Bell holds 2,869.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei measure: Yellow Bell held 2,869 grains.

sentences.zh: 萬寶常水尺律母黃鐘容黍一千三百二十。

translations.literal: Wan Baochang's water foot measure pitch mother Yellow Bell holds 1,320 millet grains.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Baochang's water-measure Yellow Bell mother pipe held 1,320 grains.

sentences.zh: 梁表、鐵尺律黃鐘副別者，其長短及口空之圍徑並同，而容黍或多或少，皆是作者旁庣其腹，使有盈虛。

translations.literal: The Liang shadow-table and iron foot measure Yellow Bell auxiliary variants—their lengths and mouth bore circumferences and diameters are all the same, but millet capacity is more or less—this is because the makers hollowed the belly on the side, creating excess or deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Liang shadow-table and iron measure Yellow Bell variants shared length and bore but differed in capacity—makers had hollowed the pipe walls unevenly.

sentences.zh: ○侯氣

translations.literal: ○ Observing Qi by Pipes
translations.idiomatic: ○ On Observing Seasonal Qi by Pitch Pipes

sentences.zh: 後齊神武霸府田曹參軍信都芳，深有巧思，能以管候氣，仰觀雲色。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Shenwu, in the regent's office as Field Office Clerk Xin Dufang, was deeply ingenious and could use pipes to observe qi, looking up to observe cloud colors.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi clerk Xin Dufang, serving Shenwu's regent office, ingeniously used pipes to observe qi and read cloud colors.

sentences.zh: 嘗與人對語，即指天曰：「孟春之氣至矣。

translations.literal: Once while conversing with someone, he pointed at Heaven and said: "The qi of early spring has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Once in conversation he pointed skyward: "Early spring qi has arrived."

sentences.zh: 」人往驗管，而飛灰已應。

translations.literal: People went to verify the pipe, and the flying ash had already responded.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors found the pipe ash already risen in response.

sentences.zh: 每月所候，言皆無爽。

translations.literal: Each month's observation was always without error.
translations.idiomatic: His monthly observations never missed.

sentences.zh: 又為輪扇二十四，埋地中，以測二十四氣。

translations.literal: He also made twenty-four wheel-fans, buried in the ground, to measure the twenty-four qi periods.
translations.idiomatic: He also built twenty-four buried wheel-fans to measure the twenty-four qi periods.

sentences.zh: 每一氣感，則一扇自動，他扇並住，與管灰相應，若符契焉。

translations.literal: When each qi period was sensed, one fan moved automatically while the others stopped, corresponding to the pipe ash like a tally.
translations.idiomatic: Each qi period activated one fan while the others stopped—matching the pipe ash like a seal and tally.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年平陳後，高祖遣毛爽及蔡子元、於普明等，以候節氣。

translations.literal: After pacifying Chen in the ninth year of Kaihuang, the High Ancestor sent Mao Shuang and Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and others to observe seasonal nodes.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Chen in Kaihuang 9, Emperor Wen sent Mao Shuang, Cai Ziyuan, and Yu Puming to observe seasonal nodes.

sentences.zh: 依古，於三重密屋之內，以木為案，十有二具。

translations.literal: Following antiquity, inside a triple-layer sealed house, wooden tables were made, twelve in number.
translations.idiomatic: Following ancient practice, twelve wooden tables were set inside a triple-walled chamber.

sentences.zh: 每取律呂之管，隨十二辰位，置於案上，而以土埋之，上平於地，中實葭莩之灰，以輕緹素覆律口。

translations.literal: Each pitch pipe and bell tone pipe, according to the twelve double-hour positions, was placed on a table and buried in earth level with the ground; inside was filled with reed-pith ash, and light silk gauze covered the pipe mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Each pitch pipe was placed on a table at its double-hour position, buried level with the ground, filled with reed-pith ash, and covered with silk gauze at the mouth.

sentences.zh: 每其月氣至，與律冥符，則灰飛沖素，蔂出於外。

translations.literal: When each month's qi arrived and matched the pitch standard in darkness, the ash flew up against the gauze and burst outward.
translations.idiomatic: When monthly qi matched the pipe, ash flew through the gauze cover.

sentences.zh: 而氣應有早晚，灰飛有多少，或初入月其氣即應；

translations.literal: But qi response had early and late times; ash flight had more or less—sometimes at the month's beginning the qi responded immediately;
translations.idiomatic: Qi responses varied in timing; ash flight varied in amount—sometimes responding at month's start,

sentences.zh: 或至中下旬間，氣始應者；

translations.literal: sometimes not until mid or late month did the qi begin to respond;
translations.idiomatic: sometimes not until mid or late month,

sentences.zh: 或灰飛出，三五夜而盡；

translations.literal: sometimes ash flew out and was exhausted in three to five nights;
translations.idiomatic: sometimes exhausting in three to five nights,

sentences.zh: 或終一月，才飛少許者。

translations.literal: or through a whole month only a little ash flew.
translations.idiomatic: or through a whole month barely rising at all.

sentences.zh: 高祖異之，以問牛弘。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor found this strange and asked Niu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was puzzled and asked Niu Hong.

sentences.zh: 弘對曰：「灰飛半出為和氣，吹灰全出為猛氣，吹灰不能出為衰氣。

translations.literal: Hong replied: "Ash flying half out is harmonious qi; blowing ash fully out is fierce qi; ash not blowing out is declining qi."
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong replied: "Half-rising ash means harmonious qi; full rising means fierce qi; no rising means declining qi."

sentences.zh: 和氣應者其政平，猛氣應者其臣縱，衰氣應者其君暴。

translations.literal: Harmonious qi responding means government is balanced; fierce qi responding means ministers are unrestrained; declining qi responding means the ruler is tyrannical."
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious qi means balanced government; fierce qi means unruly ministers; declining qi means a tyrannical ruler."

sentences.zh: 」高祖駁之曰：「臣縱君暴，其政不平，非月別而有異也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor refuted this: "Unrestrained ministers and tyrannical rulers mean unbalanced government—it is not that each month differs."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen objected: "Unruly ministers and tyrannical rulers mean bad government—it cannot vary month by month."

sentences.zh: 今十二月律，於一歲內應並不同。

translations.literal: Now the twelve monthly pitch standards within one year should all respond differently.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve monthly pipes should not all imply different political conditions within one year.

sentences.zh: 安得暴君縱臣，若斯之甚也？

translations.literal: How can there be tyrannical rulers and unrestrained ministers to such a degree?"
translations.idiomatic: How could every month signal tyranny or unruliness?"

sentences.zh: 」弘不能對。

translations.literal: Hong could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong had no answer.

sentences.zh: 令爽等草定其法。

translations.literal: Shuang and others were ordered to draft and fix the method.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Shuang and others were ordered to draft a proper method.

sentences.zh: 爽因稽諸故實，以著於篇，名曰《律譜》。

translations.literal: Shuang then examined all old records and set them forth in writing, titled the Treatise on Pitch Standards.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Shuang researched old records and wrote the Treatise on Pitch Standards.

sentences.zh: 其略云：

translations.literal: The summary says:
translations.idiomatic: In summary:

sentences.zh: 臣爽按，黃帝遣伶倫氏取竹于嶰穀，聽鳳阿閣之下，始造十二律焉。

translations.literal: Your subject Shuang reports: the Yellow Emperor sent the Ling Lun clan to take bamboo from Xie Valley; listening below the Phoenix Pavilion, they first made the twelve pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Shuang reports: the Yellow Emperor sent Ling Lun to Xie Valley for bamboo; listening at Phoenix Pavilion, he created the twelve pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 乃致天地氣應，是則數之始也。

translations.literal: Thereby the qi of Heaven and Earth responded—this is the beginning of number.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth qi responded—this was the origin of number.

sentences.zh: 陽管為律，陰管為呂，其氣以候四時，其數以紀萬物。

translations.literal: Yang pipes are pitch standards; yin pipes are bell tones; their qi observes the four seasons; their numbers record the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: Yang pipes are pitch standards, yin pipes bell tones; their qi marks the four seasons, their numbers record all things.

sentences.zh: 雲隸首作數，蓋律之本也。

translations.literal: Records say Li Shou created number—this is the root of pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou invented number—the foundation of pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 夫一、十、百、千、萬、億、兆者，引而申焉，曆度量衡，出其中矣。

translations.literal: One, ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, hundred million, and trillion—extending and expanding them, calendrical reckoning, measures, and steelyard weights emerge from within.
translations.idiomatic: One through trillion—extended further, calendars, measures, and weights all derive from them.

sentences.zh: 故有虞氏用律和聲，鄒衍改之，以定五始。

translations.literal: Therefore the Youyu clan used pitch standards to harmonize sounds; Zou Yan altered this to fix the five beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shun harmonized sounds with pitch standards; Zou Yan modified this to establish the five beginnings.

sentences.zh: 正朔服色，亦由斯而別也。

translations.literal: Correct calendar, dress, and color also differ thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar, dress, and color all followed from this.

sentences.zh: 夏正則人，殷正則地，周正則天。

translations.literal: Xia's calendar takes man as primary; Shang's takes earth; Zhou's takes Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Xia prioritized man, Shang earth, Zhou Heaven.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「吾得夏時焉。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "I obtained the Xia calendar."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "I have recovered the Xia calendar."

sentences.zh: 」謂得氣數之要矣。

translations.literal: This means he obtained the essentials of qi and number.
translations.idiomatic: Meaning he grasped the essentials of qi and number.

sentences.zh: 漢初興也，而張蒼定律，乃推五勝之法，以為水德。

translations.literal: When Han first rose, Zhang Cang fixed pitch standards and deduced the five-conquest method, taking water as the virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At Han's founding, Zhang Cang fixed pitch standards by the five-conquest method, declaring water the dominant element.

sentences.zh: 實因戰國官失其守，後秦滅學，其道浸微，蒼補綴之，未獲詳究。

translations.literal: This was because during the Warring States officials lost their posts; later Qin extinguished learning and the Way gradually declined—Cang patched and mended but did not achieve thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Warring States disorder and Qin's suppression of learning had degraded the tradition—Zhang Cang patched it without full understanding.

sentences.zh: 及孝武創制，乃置協律之官，用李延年以為都尉，頗解新聲變曲，未達音律之源，故其服色不得而定也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu created new institutions, he established the pitch-harmonizing office, appointing Li Yannian as Colonel—he understood new sounds and altered melodies but did not reach the source of pitch and pitch standards; therefore dress and color could not be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu created the pitch-harmonizing office under Li Yannian, who knew new music but not pitch theory—so dress and color remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 至於元帝，自曉音律，郎官京房，亦達其妙，因使韋玄成等雜試問房。

translations.literal: As for Emperor Yuan, he himself understood pitch and pitch standards; Palace Attendant Jing Fang also reached its subtlety; therefore Wei Xuancheng and others were sent to test Fang with mixed questions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan understood pitch himself; Jing Fang mastered its subtleties; Wei Xuancheng and others were sent to test him.

sentences.zh: 房自敘云：「學焦延壽，用六十律相生之法。

translations.literal: Fang himself narrated: "I studied under Jiao Yanshou, using the sixty pitch standards' mutual generation method."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang wrote: "I studied under Jiao Yanshou, using the sixty-standard generation method."

sentences.zh: 以上生下，皆三生二，以下生上，皆三生四。

translations.literal: Generating upward from below—all three generate two; generating downward from above—all three generate four.
translations.idiomatic: Upward generation: three produces two; downward generation: three produces four.

sentences.zh: 陽下生陰，陰上生陽，乃還相為宮之正法也。

translations.literal: Yang generating downward produces yin; yin generating upward produces yang—this is the correct method of mutual palace generation."
translations.idiomatic: Yang generates yin downward, yin generates yang upward—the proper rotating-palace method."

sentences.zh: 」于後劉歆典領條奏，著其始末，理漸研精。

translations.literal: Later Liu Xin supervised and submitted a detailed memorial, setting forth beginning and end; reason gradually became refined through study.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin later submitted a detailed memorial refining the theory.

sentences.zh: 班氏《漢志》，盡歆所出也，司馬彪《志》，並房所出也。

translations.literal: Ban's Han Treatise entirely came from Xin; Sima Biao's Treatise entirely came from Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's Treatise came entirely from Liu Xin; Sima Biao's from Jing Fang.

sentences.zh: 至於後漢，尺度稍長。

translations.literal: In Later Han, foot measures were somewhat longer.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han foot measures grew somewhat longer.

sentences.zh: 魏代杜夔，亦制律呂，以之候氣，灰悉不飛。

translations.literal: Wei's Du Kui also made pitch pipes and bell tones; using them to observe qi, the ash did not fly at all.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Du Kui made pitch pipes to observe qi—but the ash never rose.

sentences.zh: 晉光祿大夫荀勖，得古銅管，校夔所制，長古四分，方知不調，事由其誤。

translations.literal: Jin's Palace Attendant Xun Xu obtained ancient bronze pipes; comparing Kui's version, they were four fen longer than antiquity—then knowing they were out of tune; the matter arose from this error.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Xun Xu obtained ancient bronze pipes four fen longer than Du Kui's—revealing the error.

sentences.zh: 乃依《周禮》，更造古尺，用之定管，聲韻始調。

translations.literal: Thereupon following the Rites of Zhou, he remade the ancient foot measure and used it to fix the pipes; sound and pitch then harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Rites of Zhou, he remade the ancient foot measure and fixed the pipes—restoring harmony.

sentences.zh: 左晉之後，漸又訛謬。

translations.literal: After Eastern Jin, errors gradually accumulated again.
translations.idiomatic: After Eastern Jin, errors accumulated again.

sentences.zh: 至梁武帝時，猶有汲塚玉律，宋蒼梧時，鑽為橫吹，然其長短厚薄，大體具存。

translations.literal: At Liang Emperor Wu's time, there was still the jade pitch standard from the Ji tomb; in Song's Cangwu era it was drilled for transverse flutes—but its length, thickness, and breadth were largely preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Liang still had the Ji-tomb jade pitch pipe; Song drilled it for flutes but its dimensions largely survived.

sentences.zh: 臣先入棲誠，學算于祖暅，問律於何承天，沈研三紀，頗達其妙。

translations.literal: Your subject first entered Qi Cheng, studying calculation under Zu Geng and pitch standards under He Chengtian; through three cycles of deep research, I largely reached its subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: I studied calculation under Zu Geng and pitch under He Chengtian for three cycles, reaching considerable mastery.

sentences.zh: 後為太常丞，典司樂職，乃取玉管及宋太史尺，並以聞奏。

translations.literal: Later as Assistant Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, managing musical duties, I took the jade pipe and Song Grand Astrologer's foot measure and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Ceremonies assistant, I reported the jade pipe and Song astrologer's foot measure.

sentences.zh: 詔付大匠，依樣制管。

translations.literal: An edict was sent to the Master Craftsman to make pipes according to the model.
translations.idiomatic: The Master Craftsman was ordered to replicate the pipes.

sentences.zh: 自斯以後，律又飛灰。

translations.literal: From then on, pitch standards again made ash fly.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, the pipes again produced flying ash.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，臣兄喜于太樂得之。
