translations.literal: During the Hou Jing rebellion, my elder brother Xi obtained them from the Grand Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, my brother Xi recovered them from the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 後陳宣帝詣荊州為質，俄遇梁元帝敗，喜沒于周。

translations.literal: Later Chen Emperor Xuan went to Jing Province as hostage; soon encountering Liang Emperor Yuan's defeat, Xi was captured by Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's Emperor Xuan was hostage at Jingzhou; when Yuan of Liang fell, Xi was captured by Zhou.

sentences.zh: 適欲上聞，陳武帝立，遂又以十二管衍為六十律，私侯氣序，並有徵應。

translations.literal: Just as he wished to report upward, Chen Emperor Wu established the throne; he then also extended the twelve pipes to sixty pitch standards, privately observing qi sequence—all had confirming responses.
translations.idiomatic: Before reporting, Chen Wu ascended; Xi extended twelve pipes to sixty standards, privately observing qi—all confirmed.

sentences.zh: 至太建時，喜為吏部尚書，欲以聞奏。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era, Xi was Minister of Personnel and wished to report.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang, Xi as Minister of Personnel sought to report his findings.

sentences.zh: 會宣帝崩，後主嗣立，出喜為永嘉內史，遂留家內，貽諸子孫。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan died; the Later Lord succeeded; Xi was sent out as Administrator of Yongjia; he left them at home for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan died; the Later Lord sent Xi to Yongjia; he left the pipes with his family.

sentences.zh: 陳亡之際，竟並遺失。

translations.literal: At Chen's fall, they were entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: At Chen's fall, they were lost entirely.

sentences.zh: 今正十二管在太樂者，陽下生陰，始于黃鐘，陰上生陽，終於中呂，而一歲之氣，畢於此矣。

translations.literal: Now the correct twelve pipes at the Grand Music Office: yang generating yin downward begins from Yellow Bell; yin generating yang upward ends at Middle Bell Female—and one year's qi is complete herein.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve pipes at Grand Music: yang generates yin from Yellow Bell, yin generates yang to Middle Bell Female—completing the year's qi.

sentences.zh: 中呂上生執始，執始下生去滅，終於南事。

translations.literal: Middle Bell Female generates Holding the Beginning upward; Holding the Beginning generates Removing the Excess downward, ending at Southern Affair.
translations.idiomatic: Middle Bell Female generates Holding the Beginning upward; downward to Removing the Excess, ending at Southern Affair.

sentences.zh: 六十律候，畢於此矣。

translations.literal: The sixty pitch standard observations are complete herein.
translations.idiomatic: The sixty-standard qi observations end here.

sentences.zh: 仲冬之月，律中黃鐘。

translations.literal: The mid-winter month: pitch standard is Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-winter: the pitch standard is Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘者，首于冬至，陽之始也。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell begins at the winter solstice—the start of yang.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice, yang begins with Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 應天之數而長九寸，十一月氣至，則黃鐘之律應，所以宣養六氣，緝和九德也。

translations.literal: Corresponding to Heaven's number and nine cun long—when the eleventh month's qi arrives, the Yellow Bell pitch standard responds; therefore it nourishes the six qi and harmonizes the nine virtues.
translations.idiomatic: Nine cun long, matching Heaven's number—when eleventh-month qi arrives, Yellow Bell responds, nourishing the six qi and harmonizing the nine virtues.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，並用京房律准，長短宮徵，次日而用。

translations.literal: From here afterward, all use Jing Fang's pitch standard ratios; length, shortness, palace, and zhi modes are used on successive days.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all use Jing Fang's ratios; modes rotate day by day.

sentences.zh: 凡十二律，各有所攝，引而申之，至於六十。

translations.literal: All twelve pitch standards each have their domain; extending them reaches sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the twelve standards governs a domain; extended, they reach sixty.

sentences.zh: 亦由八卦衍而重之，以為六十四也。

translations.literal: This is also like the eight trigrams extended and doubled to make sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Like the eight trigrams doubled to sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 相生者相變。

translations.literal: Mutual generation means mutual transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Generation means transformation.

sentences.zh: 始黃鐘之管，下生林鐘，以陽生陰，故變也。

translations.literal: Beginning with Yellow Bell's pipe, generating Forest Bell downward—yang generating yin, therefore transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell generates Forest Bell downward—yang producing yin, hence transformation.

sentences.zh: 相攝者相通。

translations.literal: Mutual domain means mutual connection.
translations.idiomatic: Domain means connection.

sentences.zh: 如中呂之管，攝于物應，以母權子。

translations.literal: Like Middle Bell Female's pipe, domaining at Material Response—using the mother to hold the child.
translations.idiomatic: Middle Bell Female's pipe connects at Material Response—mother holding child.

sentences.zh: 故相變者，異時而各應，相通者，同月而繼應。

translations.literal: Therefore those that transform respond at different times; those that connect respond in succession within the same month.
translations.idiomatic: Transformations respond at different times; connections respond in succession within one month.

sentences.zh: 應有早晚者，非正律氣，乃子律相感，寄母中應也。

translations.literal: Responses that are early or late are not the main pitch standard qi but child standards mutually sensing, responding within the mother by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: Early or late responses come not from main standard qi but from child standards responding within the mother.

sentences.zh: 其律，大業末于江都淪喪。

translations.literal: These pitch standards were lost at Jiangdu at the end of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: These standards were lost at Jiangdu at Daye's end.

sentences.zh: ○律直日

translations.literal: ○ Pitch Standards Corresponding to Days
translations.idiomatic: ○ On Pitch Standards Corresponding to Days

sentences.zh: 宋錢樂之因京房南事之余，更生三百律。

translations.literal: Song's Qian Yuezhi, following the remainder of Jing Fang's Southern Affair, further generated three hundred pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Qian Yuezhi extended Jing Fang's Southern Affair to three hundred pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 至梁博士沈重鐘《律議》曰：「《易》以三百六十策當期之日，此律曆之數也。

translations.literal: Liang Academician Shen Chong's Discourse on Pitch Standards says: "The Changes uses 360 counting rods corresponding to the days of a period—this is the number of pitch standards and the calendar."
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Shen Chong wrote: "The Changes uses 360 rods for the days of a year—the number of pitch and calendar."

sentences.zh: 《淮南子》云：'一律而生五音，十二律而為六十音，因而六之，故三百六十音，以當一歲之日。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says: "One pitch standard generates five notes; twelve pitch standards become sixty notes; multiplying by six, therefore 360 notes correspond to the days of one year."
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi states: "One standard generates five notes; twelve standards make sixty; times six yields 360 notes for the year's days."

sentences.zh: 律曆之數，天地之道也。

translations.literal: Pitch standards and calendrical numbers are the Way of Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Pitch and calendar numbers are the Way of Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: '此則自古而然矣。

translations.literal: This has been so from antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: This has been true since antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」重乃依《淮南》本數，用京房之術求之，得三百六十律。

translations.literal: Chong then followed the Huainanzi's base number, using Jing Fang's method to seek it, obtaining 360 pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong used the Huainanzi's base number with Jing Fang's method to derive 360 standards.

sentences.zh: 各因月之本律，以為一部。

translations.literal: Each takes the root pitch standard of its month as one section.
translations.idiomatic: Each month's root pitch standard formed one section.

sentences.zh: 以一部律數為母，以一中氣所有日為子，以母命子，隨所多少，各一律所建日辰分數也。

translations.literal: Taking one section's pitch number as mother and one mid-qi period's days as child, the mother naming the child—according to how much each pitch standard's established day and double-hour fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Each section's pitch number was mother, mid-qi days child—yielding each standard's governing day and fraction.

sentences.zh: 以之分配七音，則建日冬至之聲，黃鐘為宮，太簇為商，林鐘為徵，南呂為羽，姑洗為角，應鐘為變宮，蕤賓為變徵。

translations.literal: Distributing these to the seven notes: on the winter solstice day, Yellow Bell is gong, Great Cluster shang, Forest Bell zhi, Southern Bell yu, Maiden Wash jue, Responding Bell bian gong, Luxuriant Guest bian zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Distributed to seven notes: winter solstice day—Yellow Bell gong, Great Cluster shang, Forest Bell zhi, Southern Bell yu, Maiden Wash jue, Responding Bell altered gong, Luxuriant Guest altered zhi.

sentences.zh: 五音七聲，於斯和備。

translations.literal: The five notes and seven sounds are hereby complete.
translations.idiomatic: The five notes and seven sounds were thus complete.

sentences.zh: 其次日建律，皆依次類運行。

translations.literal: The next day's pitch establishment—all follow this category in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Each subsequent governing day follows the same pattern in sequence.

sentences.zh: 當日者各自為宮，而商徵亦以次從。

translations.literal: The day itself each serves as gong, and shang and zhi also follow in order.
translations.idiomatic: Each day takes its own pitch as gong, with shang and zhi following in order.

sentences.zh: 以考聲徵氣，辨識時序，萬類所宜，各順其節。

translations.literal: Examining sound to verify qi and distinguishing time sequence—all things should each follow their season.
translations.idiomatic: Sound verifies qi and marks the seasons—each thing follows its proper period.

sentences.zh: 自黃鐘終於壯進，一百五十律，皆三分損一以下生。

translations.literal: From Yellow Bell ending at Zhuang Jin, 150 pitch standards—all generate downward by subtracting one-third.
translations.idiomatic: From Yellow Bell through Zhuang Jin, 150 standards all generate downward by subtracting one-third.

sentences.zh: 自依行終於億兆，二百九律，皆三分益一以上生。

translations.literal: From Yi Xing ending at Yi Zhao, 209 pitch standards—all generate upward by adding one-third.
translations.idiomatic: From Yi Xing through Yi Zhao, 209 standards all generate upward by adding one-third.

sentences.zh: 唯安運一律為終，不生。

translations.literal: Only An Yun as the final one does not generate.
translations.idiomatic: Only the final standard An Yun does not generate further.

sentences.zh: 其數皆取黃鐘之實十七萬七千一百四十七為本，以九三為法，各除其實，得寸分及小分，餘皆委之。

translations.literal: The numbers all take Yellow Bell's solid value 177,147 as root, using nine-cubed as divisor; each divides its solid value, obtaining cun, fen, and small fractions—the remainders are discarded.
translations.idiomatic: All calculations use Yellow Bell's base value 177,147, divided by nine-cubed, yielding cun and fen fractions—the remainder discarded.

sentences.zh: 即各其律之長也。

translations.literal: These are then the lengths of each pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: These give each pitch standard's length.

sentences.zh: 修其律部，則上生下生宮徵之次也。

translations.literal: Arranging the pitch sections gives the order of upward generation, downward generation, gong, and zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Arranging the pitch sections yields the order of generation and modal succession.

sentences.zh: 今略其名次雲。

translations.literal: Now the names and order are briefly listed below.
translations.idiomatic: The names and order are listed below.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘：

translations.literal: Yellow Bell:
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell section:

sentences.zh: 包育含微帝德廣運下濟克終執始握鑒持樞黃中通聖潛升

translations.literal: Bao Yu, Han Wei, Di De, Guang Yun, Xia Ji, Ke Zhong, Zhi Shi, Wo Jian, Chi Shu, Huang Zhong, Tong Sheng, Qian Sheng
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yu, Han Wei, Di De, Guang Yun, Xia Ji, Ke Zhong, Zhi Shi, Wo Jian, Chi Shu, Huang Zhong, Tong Sheng, Qian Sheng, and others

sentences.zh: 殷普景盛滋萌光被咸亨乃文乃聖微陽分動生氣雲繁鬱湮

translations.literal: Yin Pu, Jing Sheng, Zi Meng, Guang Bei, Xian Heng, Nai Wen, Nai Sheng, Wei Yang, Fen Dong, Sheng Qi, Yun Fan, Yu
translations.idiomatic: Yin Pu, Jing Sheng, Zi Meng, Guang Bei, Xian Heng, Nai Wen, Nai Sheng, Wei Yang, Fen Dong, Sheng Qi, Yun Fan, Yu, and others

sentences.zh: 升引屯結開元質未僾昧逋建玄中玉燭調風

translations.literal: Sheng Yin, Tun Jie, Kai Yuan, Zhi Wei, Qian Mei, Yu Jian, Xuan Zhong, Yu Zhu, Diao Feng
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yin, Tun Jie, Kai Yuan, Zhi Wei, Qian Mei, Yu Jian, Xuan Zhong, Yu Zhu, and Diao Feng

sentences.zh: 右黃鐘一部，三十四律。

translations.literal: Right: Yellow Bell section, thirty-four pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell section: thirty-four pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 每律直三十四分日之三十一

translations.literal: Each pitch standard governs thirty-four parts of thirty-one parts of a day.
translations.idiomatic: Each standard governs thirty-four thirty-firsts of a day.

sentences.zh: 大呂：

translations.literal: Great Bell:
translations.idiomatic: Great Bell section:

sentences.zh: 荄動始贊大有坤元輔時匡弼分否又繁唯微棄望庶幾執義秉強陵陰侶陽識沈緝熙知道適時權變少出阿衡同雲承明善述休光

translations.literal: Gai Dong, Shi Zan, Da You, Kun Yuan, Fu Shi, Kuang Bi, Fen Fou, You Fan, Wei Wei, Qi Wang, Shu Yi, Bing Qiang, Ling Yin, Lu Yang, Shi Shen, Ji Xi, Zhi Dao, Shi Shi, Quan Bian, Tong Yun, Cheng Ming, Shan Shu, Xiu Guang
translations.idiomatic: Gai Dong, Shi Zan, Da You, Kun Yuan, Fu Shi, Kuang Bi, Fen Fou, You Fan, Wei Wei, Qi Wang, Shu Yi, Bing Qiang, and twenty-one others

sentences.zh: 右大呂一部，二十七律。

translations.literal: Right: Great Bell section, twenty-seven pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Great Bell section: twenty-seven pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 每律直一日及二十七分日之三

translations.literal: Each pitch standard governs one day and three twenty-sevenths of a day.
translations.idiomatic: Each standard governs one day plus three twenty-sevenths of a day.

sentences.zh: 太簇：

translations.literal: Great Cluster:

sentences.zh: 《史記》曰：「夏禹以身為度，以聲為律。

translations.literal: The Records of the Grand Historian says: "Yu of Xia used his body as measure and sound as pitch standard."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian records: "Yu of Xia used his body for measure and sound for pitch."

sentences.zh: 」《禮記》曰：「丈夫布手為尺。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says: "A man's outstretched hand is the foot measure."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites states: "A man's outstretched hand defines the foot measure."

sentences.zh: 」《周官》云：「璧羨起度。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou says: "The jade surplus begins measure."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou says: "The jade surplus initiates measure."

sentences.zh: 」鄭司農云：「羨，長也。

translations.literal: Zheng Sizhong says: "Surplus means length."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sizhong explains: "Surplus means length."

sentences.zh: 此璧徑尺，以起度量。

translations.literal: This jade disk is one chi in diameter, to begin measures.
translations.idiomatic: This one-chi-diameter jade disk establishes all measures.

sentences.zh: 」《易緯通卦驗》：「十馬尾為一分。

translations.literal: The Changes Weft, Comprehensive Hexagram Verification: "Ten horse tails make one fen."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes Weft states: "Ten horse-tail widths make one fen."

sentences.zh: 」《淮南子》云：「秋分而禾緌定，緌定而禾熟。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says: "At the autumn equinox the grain awns are fixed; when awns are fixed the grain ripens."
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says: "At the autumn equinox grain awns set; when awns set, grain ripens."

sentences.zh: 律數十二而當一粟，十二粟而當一寸。

translations.literal: Pitch number twelve corresponds to one millet grain; twelve millet grains correspond to one cun."
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pitch numbers equal one millet grain; twelve grains equal one cun."

sentences.zh: 」緌者，禾穗芒也。

translations.literal: Awn means the grain ear's bristle.
translations.idiomatic: Awn refers to the grain ear's bristle.

sentences.zh: 《說苑》云：「度量權衡以粟生，一粟為一分。

translations.literal: The Garden of Persuasions says: "Steelyard, measures, and weights arise from millet—one millet grain is one fen."
translations.idiomatic: The Garden of Persuasions states: "Weights and measures derive from millet—one grain equals one fen."

sentences.zh: 」《孫子算術》云：「蠶所生吐絲為忽，十忽為秒，十秒為毫，十毫為厘，十厘為分。

translations.literal: The Sunzi Calculation Methods says: "What the silkworm produces and spits as thread is a hu; ten hu make a miao; ten miao make a hao; ten hao make a li; ten li make a fen."
translations.idiomatic: The Sunzi Calculation Methods defines: silkworm thread is a hu; ten hu a miao; ten miao a hao; ten hao a li; ten li a fen.

sentences.zh: 」此皆起度之源，其文舛互。

translations.literal: These are all origins of measure; the texts conflict.
translations.idiomatic: These are all origins of measure—but the texts conflict.

sentences.zh: 唯《漢志》：「度者，所以度長短也，本起黃鐘之長。

translations.literal: Only the Han Treatise: "Measure is what measures length and shortness; it originates from Yellow Bell's length."
translations.idiomatic: Only the Han Treatise is authoritative: "Measure gauges length, originating from Yellow Bell's length."

sentences.zh: 以子穀秬黍中者，一黍之廣度之，九十黍為黃鐘之長。

translations.literal: Using black millet grains of medium size, measuring one grain's breadth—ninety grains make Yellow Bell's length.
translations.idiomatic: Using medium black millet grains, one grain's width measured—ninety grains equal Yellow Bell's length.

sentences.zh: 一黍為一分，十分為一寸，十寸為一尺，十尺為一丈，十丈為一引，而五度審矣。

translations.literal: One grain is one fen; ten fen one cun; ten cun one chi; ten chi one zhang; ten zhang one yin—and the five measures are verified.
translations.idiomatic: One grain one fen; ten fen one cun; ten cun one chi; ten chi one zhang; ten zhang one yin—the five measures verified.

sentences.zh: 」後之作者，又憑此說，以律度量衡，並因秬黍散為諸法，其率可通故也。

translations.literal: Later makers also relied on this theory; pitch standards, measures, and steelyard weights all derive black millet scattered into various methods—their ratios are commensurable.
translations.idiomatic: Later makers followed this theory—pitch, measure, and weight all derived from black millet with commensurable ratios.

sentences.zh: 黍有大小之差，年有豐耗之異，前代量校，每有不同，又俗傳訛替，漸致增損。

translations.literal: Millet has differences of large and small; years have differences of abundance and scarcity; previous ages' measure comparisons each differ; also popular transmission errs and gradually causes increase and decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Millet varies in size, harvests vary in yield, and each age's calibrations differ—popular error gradually altered the standards.

sentences.zh: 今略諸代尺度一十五等，並異同之說如左。

translations.literal: Now fifteen grades of foot measures of various dynasties are briefly listed, with explanations of differences and similarities as follows.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen grades of historical foot measures are listed below with their differences.

sentences.zh: 一、周尺

translations.literal: One: Zhou foot measure
translations.idiomatic: I. Zhou foot measure

sentences.zh: 《漢志》王莽時劉歆銅斛尺。

translations.literal: The Han Treatise: Liu Xin's copper hu foot measure from Wang Mang's time.
translations.idiomatic: Han Treatise: Liu Xin's copper hu measure from Wang Mang's era.

sentences.zh: 後漢建武銅尺。

translations.literal: Later Han Jianwu copper foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han Jianwu copper measure.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始十年荀勖律尺，為晉前尺。

translations.literal: Jin Taishi tenth year Xun Xu pitch foot measure—the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Taishi 10 Xun Xu pitch measure—the pre-Jin standard.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之所傳銅尺。

translations.literal: The copper foot measure transmitted by Zu Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi's transmitted copper foot measure.

sentences.zh: 徐廣、徐爰、王隱等《晉書》云：「武帝泰始九年，中書監荀勖校太樂八音，不和，始知為後漢至魏，尺長於古四分有餘。

translations.literal: Xu Guang, Xu Ai, Wang Yin, and others' Jin History says: "In Emperor Wu's Taishi ninth year, Director of the Secretariat Xun Xu corrected the Grand Music eight timbres—they were not harmonious; then knowing that from Later Han through Wei the foot measure was more than four fen longer than antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Jin History records: in Taishi 9, Xun Xu found the eight timbres discordant—the Wei measure exceeded antiquity by four fen.

sentences.zh: 勖乃部著作郎劉恭，依《周禮》制尺，所謂古尺也。

translations.literal: Xu then ordered Editorial Director Liu Gong to make a foot measure according to the Rites of Zhou—the so-called ancient foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xu ordered Liu Gong to make a Rites of Zhou foot measure—the ancient standard.

sentences.zh: 依古尺更鑄銅律呂，以調聲韻。

translations.literal: According to the ancient foot measure, bronze pitch pipes and bell tones were recast to tune sound and pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Using the ancient measure, bronze pitch pipes were recast to restore harmony.

sentences.zh: 以尺量古器，與本銘尺寸無差。

translations.literal: Using the foot measure to measure ancient vessels, there was no discrepancy with original inscription dimensions.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient vessels measured against it matched their inscriptions exactly.

sentences.zh: 又汲郡盜發魏襄王塚，得古周時玉律及鐘磬，與新律聲韻暗同。

translations.literal: Also the Ji commandery tomb robbers opened King Xiang of Wei's tomb, obtaining ancient Zhou jade pitch standards and bells and chime stones—their sound and pitch darkly matched the new pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Ji commandery tomb robbers found Zhou jade pitch pipes and bells matching the new standards.

sentences.zh: 于時郡國或得漢時故鐘，吹新律命之，皆應。

translations.literal: At the time in commanderies and kingdoms, Han-era old bells were sometimes obtained; blowing the new pitch standards to tune them—all responded.
translations.idiomatic: Han-era bells found in the provinces all matched when tested against the new pipes.

sentences.zh: 」梁武《鐘律緯》云：「祖沖之所傳銅尺，其銘曰：'晉泰始十年，中書考古器，揆校今尺，長四分半。

translations.literal: Liang Wu's Treatise on Bell Standards and Pitch Pipes says: "The copper foot measure transmitted by Zu Chongzhi—its inscription says: 'Jin Taishi tenth year, the Secretariat examined ancient vessels and compared the present foot measure—it is four fen and a half longer."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu's Treatise cites Zu Chongzhi's copper measure: "Jin Taishi 10—four fen and a half longer than the present measure."

sentences.zh: 所校古法有七品：一曰姑洗玉律，二曰小呂玉律，三曰西京銅望臬，四曰金錯望臬，五曰銅斛，六曰古錢，七曰建武銅尺。

translations.literal: The ancient methods examined had seven grades: first, Maiden Wash jade pitch standard; second, Lesser Bell jade pitch standard; third, Western Capital bronze gnomon table; fourth, gold-inlaid gnomon table; fifth, copper hu; sixth, ancient coins; seventh, Jianwu copper foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Seven ancient reference standards were tested: Maiden Wash jade pipe, Lesser Bell jade pipe, Western Capital bronze gnomon, gold-inlaid gnomon, copper hu, ancient coins, and Jianwu copper measure.

sentences.zh: 姑洗微強，西京望臬微弱，其餘與此尺同。

translations.literal: Maiden Wash was slightly strong; Western Capital gnomon table slightly weak—the rest matched this foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Maiden Wash ran slightly high; the Western Capital gnomon slightly low—the rest matched.

sentences.zh: '銘八十二字。

translations.literal: Inscription: eighty-two characters.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription contains eighty-two characters.

sentences.zh: 此尺者，勖新尺也。

translations.literal: This foot measure is Xu's new foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: This is Xu's new measure.

sentences.zh: 今尺者，杜夔尺也。

translations.literal: Today's foot measure is Du Kui's foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: The contemporary measure is Du Kui's.

sentences.zh: 雷次宗、何胤之二人作《鐘律圖》，所載荀勖校量古尺文，與此銘同。

translations.literal: Lei Cizong and He Yin's two authors' Diagram of Bell Standards and Pitch Pipes records Xun Xu's examination text of the ancient foot measure—the same as this inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Cizong and He Yin's Diagram records the same Xun Xu examination text.

sentences.zh: 而蕭吉樂譜，謂為梁朝所考七品，謬也。

translations.literal: But Xiao Ji's Music Treatise calls it the seven grades examined by the Liang court—this is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji wrongly attributes these to Liang-era examination.

sentences.zh: 今以此尺為本，以校諸代尺」雲。

translations.literal: Now taking this foot measure as base to compare foot measures of various dynasties."
translations.idiomatic: This measure serves as the base for comparing all dynastic foot measures."

sentences.zh: 二、晉田父玉尺

translations.literal: Two: Jin farmer's jade foot measure
translations.idiomatic: II. Jin farmer's jade foot measure

sentences.zh: 梁法尺，實比晉前尺一尺七厘。

translations.literal: The Liang legal foot measure is actually one chi seven li longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Liang legal measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi seven li.

sentences.zh: 《世說》稱，有田父于野地中得周時玉尺，便是天下正尺。

translations.literal: Tales of the World says a farmer in the fields obtained a Zhou jade foot measure—this was the realm's correct foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Tales of the World tells of a farmer finding a Zhou jade measure—the realm's true standard.

sentences.zh: 荀勖試以校尺，所造金石絲竹，皆短校一米。

translations.literal: Xun Xu tested it to compare foot measures; metal, stone, silk, and bamboo all came out one meter short in comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu tested it—all metal, stone, silk, and bamboo instruments proved one meter short.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝《鐘律緯稱》，主衣從上相承，有周時銅尺一枚，古玉律八枚。

translations.literal: Liang Emperor Wu's Treatise on Bell Standards and Pitch Pipes states that from the Master of Robes' transmitted succession there was one Zhou copper foot measure and eight ancient jade pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu's Treatise records one Zhou copper measure and eight jade pitch pipes from the Master of Robes.

sentences.zh: 檢主衣周尺，東昏用為章信，尺不復存。

translations.literal: Examining the Master of Robes' Zhou foot measure—Emperor Donghun used it as a seal credential; the foot measure no longer survives.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Robes' Zhou measure was used as Emperor Donghun's seal credential—it no longer survives.

sentences.zh: 玉律一囗蕭，餘定七枚夾鐘，有昔題刻。

translations.literal: One jade pitch standard damaged; the remaining seven fixed as Pinched Bell have old inscription carvings.
translations.idiomatic: One jade pipe was damaged; seven Pinched Bell pipes with old inscriptions remain.

sentences.zh: 乃制為尺，以相參驗。

translations.literal: Thereupon a foot measure was made to cross-verify.
translations.idiomatic: A foot measure was made for cross-verification.

sentences.zh: 取細毫中黍，積次詶定，今之最為詳密，長祖沖之尺校半分。

translations.literal: Taking fine-haired medium millet, accumulating and fixing by repeated measurement—today's is most detailed and precise, half a fen longer than Zu Chongzhi's foot measure in comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Fine-haired medium millet was accumulated for precise calibration—half a fen longer than Zu Chongzhi's measure.

sentences.zh: 以新尺制為四器，名為通。

translations.literal: Using the new foot measure, four instruments were made, called the Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Four Tong instruments were made from the new measure.

sentences.zh: 又依新尺為笛，以命古鐘，按刻夷則，以笛命飲和韻，夷則定合。

translations.literal: Also according to the new foot measure, flutes were made; using them to tune ancient bells—inscription carved Luxuriant Guest; using the flute to tune, harmony and pitch—Luxuriant Guest was fixed as matching.
translations.idiomatic: Flutes from the new measure tuned ancient bells inscribed Luxuriant Guest—confirming the match.

sentences.zh: 案此兩尺長短近同。

translations.literal: Examining these two foot measures—their lengths are nearly the same.
translations.idiomatic: These two measures are nearly identical in length.

sentences.zh: 三、梁表尺實比晉前尺一尺二分二厘一毫有奇。

translations.literal: Three: Liang shadow-table foot measure is actually one chi two fen two li one hao and a fraction longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: III. Liang shadow-table measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi two fen two li one hao and a fraction.

sentences.zh: 蕭吉云：「出於《司馬法》。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji says: "It comes from the Sima Methods."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji attributes it to the Sima Methods.

sentences.zh: 梁朝刻其度於影表，以測影。

translations.literal: The Liang court carved its measure on the shadow table to measure shadows.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang court carved its measure on a gnomon table for shadow measurement.

sentences.zh: 」案此即奉朝請祖暅所算造銅主影表者也。

translations.literal: Examining this—it is the bronze gnomon shadow table calculated and made by Court Gentleman Zu Geng.
translations.idiomatic: This is Court Gentleman Zu Geng's calculated bronze gnomon table.

sentences.zh: 經陳滅入朝。

translations.literal: After Chen's fall it entered the court.
translations.idiomatic: It entered the court after Chen's fall.

sentences.zh: 大業中，議以合古，乃用之調律，以制鐘磬等八音樂器。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, discussion held it accorded with antiquity; therefore it was used to tune pitch standards and make bells, chime stones, and the eight timbres.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye, it was deemed most antiquity-conforming and used to tune bells, chimes, and the eight timbres.

sentences.zh: 四、漢官尺實比晉前尺一尺三分七毫。

translations.literal: Four: Han official foot measure is actually one chi three fen seven hao longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: IV. Han official measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi three fen seven hao.

sentences.zh: 晉時始平掘地得古銅尺。

translations.literal: In Jin times, excavating the ground at Shiping obtained an ancient copper foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: At Shiping during Jin, excavations yielded an ancient copper foot measure.

sentences.zh: 蕭吉《樂譜》云：「漢章帝時，零陵文學史奚景於泠道縣舜廟下得玉律，度為此尺。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji's Music Treatise says: "In Emperor Zhang of Han's time, Lingling Literary Scholar Xi Jing at Shun's temple in Lengdao county obtained a jade pitch standard and made this foot measure from it."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji records: Han Zhangdi's scholar Xi Jing found a jade pipe at Shun's temple in Lengdao and derived this measure.

sentences.zh: 」傅暢《晉諸公贊》云：「葛勖造鐘律，時人並稱其精密，唯陳留阮鹹，譏其聲高。

translations.literal: Fu Chang's Jin Worthies' Praise says: "Ge Xun made bell and pitch standards; people all praised their precision—only Chenliu Ruan Xian criticized their sound as high."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang records: Ge Xun's standards were praised for precision—only Ruan Xian of Chenliu criticized the pitch as too high.

sentences.zh: 後始平掘地，得古銅尺，歲久欲腐，以校荀勖今尺，短校四分。

translations.literal: Later at Shiping, excavating the ground, an ancient copper foot measure was obtained—long decayed; comparing with Xun Xu's present foot measure, it was four fen shorter in comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Shiping, a decayed ancient copper measure proved four fen shorter than Xun Xu's—vindicating Ruan Xian.

sentences.zh: 時人以咸為解。

translations.literal: People of the time took Xian as having understood.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries acknowledged Ruan Xian was correct.

sentences.zh: 」此兩尺長短近同。

translations.literal: These two foot measures' lengths are nearly the same.
translations.idiomatic: These two measures are nearly identical.

sentences.zh: 五、魏尺杜夔所用調律，比晉前尺一尺四分七厘。

translations.literal: Five: Wei foot measure used by Du Kui for tuning pitch standards—one chi four fen seven li longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: V. Du Kui's Wei tuning measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi four fen seven li.

sentences.zh: 魏陳留王景元四年，劉徽注《九章》雲，王莽時劉歆斛尺，弱於今尺四分五厘，比魏尺，其斛深九寸五分五厘。

translations.literal: Wei's Prince of Chenliu, Jingyuan fourth year—Liu Hui's commentary on the Nine Chapters says Liu Xin's hu foot measure from Wang Mang's time was four fen five li weaker than today's foot measure; compared with Wei's foot measure, its hu depth was nine cun five fen five li.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui noted Wang Mang's hu measure was four fen five li shorter; Wei's hu depth was nine cun five fen five li.

sentences.zh: 即晉荀勖所雲「杜夔尺長於今尺四分半」是也。

translations.literal: This is what Jin's Xun Xu said: "Du Kui's foot measure is four fen and a half longer than today's foot measure."
translations.idiomatic: This confirms Xun Xu's statement that Du Kui's measure exceeded the contemporary by four fen and a half.

sentences.zh: 六、晉後尺實比晉前尺一尺六分二厘。

translations.literal: Six: Post-Jin foot measure is actually one chi six fen two li longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: VI. Post-Jin measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi six fen two li.

sentences.zh: 蕭吉雲，晉氏江東所用。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji says the Jin clan used this in Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji says Eastern Jin used this measure in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 七、後魏前尺實比晉前尺一尺二寸七厘。

translations.literal: Seven: Northern Wei early foot measure is actually one chi two cun seven li longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: VII. Northern Wei early measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi two cun seven li.

sentences.zh: 八、中尺實比晉前尺一尺二寸一分一厘。

translations.literal: Eight: Middle foot measure is actually one chi two cun one fen one li longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: VIII. Middle measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi two cun one fen one li.

sentences.zh: 九、後尺實比晉前尺一尺二寸八分一厘。

translations.literal: Nine: Later foot measure is actually one chi two cun eight fen one li longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: IX. Later measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi two cun eight fen one li.

sentences.zh: 即開皇官尺及後周市尺

translations.literal: This is the Kaihuang official foot measure and Northern Zhou market foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: These are the Kaihuang official and Northern Zhou market measures.

sentences.zh: 後周市尺，比玉尺一尺九分三厘。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou market foot measure is one chi nine fen three li longer than the jade foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou market measure exceeds the jade measure by one chi nine fen three li.

sentences.zh: 開皇官尺，即鐵尺，一尺二寸。

translations.literal: Kaihuang official foot measure, which is the iron foot measure—one chi two cun.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang official measure—the iron measure—is one chi two cun.

sentences.zh: 此後魏初及東西分國，後周未用玉尺之前，雜用此等尺。

translations.literal: This was used miscellaneously during early Northern Wei and the east-west division of states, before Northern Zhou used the jade foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: These were used during early Northern Wei and before Northern Zhou adopted the jade measure.

sentences.zh: 甄鸞《算術》云：「周朝市尺，得玉尺九分二厘。

translations.literal: Zhen Luan's Calculation Methods says: "Northern Zhou market foot measure obtained the jade foot measure's nine fen two li."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Luan records: Northern Zhou market measure equaled nine fen two li of the jade measure.

sentences.zh: 」或傳梁時有志公道人作此尺，寄入周朝；

translations.literal: Some transmit that during Liang times a Daoist named Zhi Gongdao made this foot measure and sent it into the Zhou court;
translations.idiomatic: Tradition holds a Liang Daoist Zhi Gongdao made this measure and sent it to Zhou;

sentences.zh: 雲與多須老翁。

translations.literal: saying it matched the old man Duoxu.
translations.idiomatic: claiming it matched the elder Duoxu.

sentences.zh: 周太祖及隋高祖，各自以為謂己。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou's Taizu and Sui's Gaozu each thought it referred to themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Taizu and Sui's Gaozu each thought it referred to himself.

sentences.zh: 周朝人間行用。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou common people used it in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou commoners used it in daily life.

sentences.zh: 及開皇初，著令以為官尺，百司用之，終於仁壽。

translations.literal: At Kaihuang's beginning, an order established it as the official foot measure; the hundred offices used it until Renshou.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang made it the official measure, used by all offices until Renshou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，人間或私用之。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, people sometimes used it privately.
translations.idiomatic: Daye saw occasional private use.

sentences.zh: 十、東後魏尺實比晉前尺一尺五寸八毫。

translations.literal: Ten: Eastern Northern Wei foot measure is actually one chi five cun eight hao longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: X. Eastern Northern Wei measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi five cun eight hao.

sentences.zh: 此是魏中尉元延明累黍用半周之廣為尺，齊朝因而用之。

translations.literal: This is what Wei's Commandant of the Palace Guard Yuan Yanming made by accumulating millet, using half Zhou's breadth as foot measure—the Qi court therefore used it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Commandant Yuan Yanming made this by accumulating millet at half Zhou breadth—adopted by Qi.

sentences.zh: 魏收《魏史·律曆志》云：「公孫崇永平中更造新尺，以一黍之長，累為寸法。

translations.literal: Wei Shou's Wei History Treatise on Pitch Standards and the Calendar says: "Gongsun Chong in the Yongping era again made a new foot measure, accumulating cun method from one millet grain's length."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou records: Gongsun Chong remade the measure in Yongping, accumulating cun from one millet grain's length.

sentences.zh: 尋太常卿劉芳受詔修樂，以秬黍中者一黍之廣，即為一分。

translations.literal: Soon Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Fang received an edict to repair music; using black millet grains of medium size, one grain's breadth was one fen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master Liu Fang used medium black millet—one grain's width as one fen.

sentences.zh: 而中尉元匡，以一黍之廣度黍二縫，以取一分。

translations.literal: But Commandant Yuan Kuang, using one millet grain's breadth to measure two millet grain seams, took one fen.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Yuan Kuang measured two grain seams for one fen.

sentences.zh: 三家紛競，久不能決。

translations.literal: Three families disputed, unable to decide for long.
translations.idiomatic: Three factions disputed without resolution.

sentences.zh: 大和十九年高祖詔，以一黍之廣，用成分體，九十之黍，黃鐘之長，以定銅尺。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taihe, the High Ancestor edicted: using one millet grain's breadth to make fen units, ninety grains for Yellow Bell's length, to fix the copper foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 19, the emperor ordered: one grain's width as fen, ninety grains for Yellow Bell's length, fixing the copper measure.

sentences.zh: 有司奏從前詔，而芳尺同高祖所制，故遂典修金石。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized following the previous edict; Fang's foot measure matched the High Ancestor's making—therefore he managed metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's measure matched the imperial standard—he was charged with metal and stone instruments.

sentences.zh: 迄武定未有論律者。

translations.literal: Until Wuding no one discussed pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: No pitch discussion occurred until Wuding.

translations.literal: End quotation.
translations.idiomatic: End of quotation.

sentences.zh: 十一、蔡邕銅籥尺

translations.literal: Eleven: Cai Yong's copper pitch key foot measure
translations.idiomatic: XI. Cai Yong's copper pitch key measure

sentences.zh: 後周玉尺，實比晉前尺一尺一寸五分八厘。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou jade foot measure is actually one chi one cun five fen eight li longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou jade measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi one cun five fen eight li.

sentences.zh: 從上相承，有銅籥一，以銀錯題，其銘曰：「籥，黃鐘之宮，長九寸，空圍九分，容秬黍一千二百粒，稱重十二銖，兩之為一合。

translations.literal: From transmitted succession, there is one copper pitch key with silver inscription; its inscription says: "Key—Yellow Bell palace pitch, nine cun long, bore circumference nine fen, holds 1,200 black millet grains, weighs twelve zhu, two make one he."
translations.idiomatic: A transmitted copper pitch key bears silver inscription: "Yellow Bell palace pitch, nine cun, bore nine fen circumference, 1,200 black millet grains, twelve zhu weight, two he per pair."

sentences.zh: 三分損益，轉生十二律。

translations.literal: Adding or subtracting one-third in rotation generates the twelve pitch standards."
translations.idiomatic: Tripling or dividing by three generates the twelve standards."

sentences.zh: 」祖孝孫云：「相承傳是蔡邕銅籥。

translations.literal: Zu Xiaosun says: "Transmitted succession holds this is Cai Yong's copper pitch key."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaosun identifies it as Cai Yong's transmitted copper pitch key.

translations.literal: End quotation.
translations.idiomatic: End of inscription.

sentences.zh: 後周武帝保定中，詔遣大宗伯盧景宣、上党公長孫紹遠、岐國公斛斯徵等，累黍造尺，從橫不定。

translations.literal: In Northern Zhou Emperor Wu's Baoding era, an edict sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Jingxuan, Duke of Shangdang Changsun Shaoyuan, Duke of Qi Guo Husizheng, and others to accumulate millet and make a foot measure—the transverse and longitudinal undetermined.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding era, Lu Jingxuan, Changsun Shaoyuan, and Husizheng were ordered to accumulate millet for a new measure—but dimensions remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 後因修倉掘地，得古玉鬥，以為正器，據鬥造律度量衡。

translations.literal: Later while repairing a granary, excavating the ground, an ancient jade dipper was obtained and taken as the correct vessel; according to the dipper, pitch standards, measures, and steelyard weights were made.
translations.idiomatic: Repairing a granary yielded an ancient jade dipper used to make pitch pipes, measures, and weights.

sentences.zh: 因用此尺，大赦，改元天和，百司行用，終於大象之末。

translations.literal: Therefore this foot measure was used; great amnesty, era name changed to Tianhe; the hundred offices used it until the end of Daxiang.
translations.idiomatic: This measure was adopted with a Tianhe era amnesty, used until Daxiang's end.

sentences.zh: 其律黃鐘，與蔡邕古籥同。

translations.literal: Its Yellow Bell pitch standard matches Cai Yong's ancient pitch key.
translations.idiomatic: Its Yellow Bell matched Cai Yong's ancient pitch key.

sentences.zh: 十二、宋氏尺實比晉前尺一尺六分四厘。

translations.literal: Twelve: Song foot measure is actually one chi six fen four li longer than the pre-Jin foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: XII. Song measure exceeds pre-Jin by one chi six fen four li.

sentences.zh: 錢樂之渾天儀尺。

translations.literal: Qian Yuezhi's armillary sphere foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yuezhi's armillary sphere measure.

sentences.zh: 後周鐵尺。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou iron foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou iron measure.

sentences.zh: 開皇初調鐘律尺及平陳後調鐘律水尺。

translations.literal: Kaihuang initial bell-and-pitch-standard foot measure and post-Chen-pacification water foot measure for bell and pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang bell-tuning measure and post-Chen water measure.

sentences.zh: 此宋代人間所用尺，傳入齊、梁、陳，以制樂律。

translations.literal: This is the foot measure Song common people used, transmitted into Qi, Liang, and Chen to make musical pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Song's popular measure passed through Qi, Liang, and Chen for musical standards.

sentences.zh: 與晉後尺及梁時俗尺、劉曜渾天儀尺，略相依近。

translations.literal: With post-Jin foot measure and Liang popular foot measure and Liu Yao's armillary sphere foot measure, it is slightly close in dependency.
translations.idiomatic: It closely resembles post-Jin, Liang popular, and Liu Yao armillary measures.

sentences.zh: 當由人間恆用，增損訛替之所致也。

translations.literal: This must be because common people constantly used it, causing increase, decrease, error, and replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Constant popular use caused gradual distortion.

sentences.zh: 周建德六年平齊後，即以此同律度量，頒於天下。

translations.literal: After Northern Zhou Jiande sixth year pacified Qi, immediately using this same pitch standard measure, it was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiande 6 pacified Qi, this standard was promulgated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 其後宣帝時，達奚震及牛弘等議曰：

translations.literal: Later in Emperor Xuan's time, Daxi Zhen and Niu Hong and others memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Later under Emperor Xuan, Daxi Zhen and Niu Hong submitted:

sentences.zh: 竊惟權衡度量，經邦懋軌，誠須詳求故實，考校得衷。

translations.literal: We humbly consider steelyard, measures, and weights—the canonical track of governing the state; truly one must seek old reality in detail and examine and compare to obtain the center.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that weights and measures are foundational to governance—requiring thorough examination of historical evidence.

sentences.zh: 謹尋今之鐵尺，是太祖遣尚書故蘇綽所造，當時檢勘，用為前周之尺。

translations.literal: Respectfully seeking: today's iron foot measure was made by the late Minister of Works Su Chuo sent by the Taizu; at the time of inspection it was used as Former Zhou's foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Today's iron measure was made by the late Su Chuo for Taizu, verified as Former Zhou's standard.

sentences.zh: 驗其長短，與宋尺符同，即以調鐘律，並用均田度地。

translations.literal: Verifying its length and shortness, it matches the Song foot measure; immediately using it to tune bell and pitch standards, and also using it for equal-field land measurement.
translations.idiomatic: It matches the Song measure—used for pitch tuning and equal-field land measurement.

sentences.zh: 今以上黨羊頭山黍，依《漢書·律曆志》度之。

translations.literal: Now using Shangdang Yangtou Mountain millet, measuring according to the Han Treatise on Pitch Standards and the Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: We now measure using Shangdang Yangtou Mountain millet per the Han Treatise.

sentences.zh: 若以大者稠累，依數滿尺，實于黃鐘之律，須撼乃容。

translations.literal: If using large grains densely accumulated, filling the foot measure by number—in Yellow Bell's pitch standard one must shake to contain them.
translations.idiomatic: Large grains densely packed require shaking to fill Yellow Bell's pipe.

sentences.zh: 若以中者累尺，雖複小稀，實于黃鐘之律，不動而滿。

translations.literal: If using medium grains accumulated to foot measure—though somewhat sparse, in Yellow Bell's pitch standard they fill without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Medium grains fill Yellow Bell's pipe without shaking.

sentences.zh: 計此二事之殊，良由消息未善，其於鐵尺，終有一會。

translations.literal: Calculating this difference between the two matters—truly because the message was not yet good; as for the iron foot measure, there will ultimately be one meeting point.
translations.idiomatic: This discrepancy suggests imperfect calibration—but the iron measure will ultimately prove correct.

sentences.zh: 且上黨之黍，有異他鄉，其色至烏，其形圓重，用之為量，定不徒然。

translations.literal: Moreover Shangdang's millet differs from other regions—its color is extremely black, its shape round and heavy; using it as measure, it is certainly not in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Shangdang millet differs from other regions—black, round, and heavy—making a reliable standard.

sentences.zh: 正以時有水旱之差，地有肥瘠之異，取黍大小，未必得中。

translations.literal: Precisely because at times there are differences of flood and drought, and lands have differences of fertility and barrenness, taking millet large or small, one may not necessarily obtain the center.
translations.idiomatic: Harvest and soil variations mean medium-sized grains may not always be obtainable.

sentences.zh: 案許慎解，秬黍體大，本異于常。

translations.literal: Examining Xu Shen's explanation: black millet body is large, fundamentally different from ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen notes black millet is inherently larger than ordinary grain.

sentences.zh: 疑今之大者，正是其中，累百滿尺，即是會古。

translations.literal: Suspecting today's large ones are precisely the medium ones—accumulating a hundred filling the foot measure is meeting antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Today's large grains may be the true medium—one hundred filling the measure matches antiquity.

sentences.zh: 賓籥之外，才剩十餘，此恐圍徑或差，造律未妙。

translations.literal: Beyond the guest pitch key, only ten-odd remain—this fears bore circumference or diameter may differ, making pitch standards not subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the guest key, only ten-odd grains remain—perhaps bore circumference is slightly off.

sentences.zh: 就如撼動取滿，論理亦通。

translations.literal: Even like shaking to take full measure, speaking in principle it also passes.
translations.idiomatic: Even requiring shaking to fill, the principle still holds.

sentences.zh: 今勘周漢古錢，大小有合，宋氏渾儀，尺度無舛。

translations.literal: Now examining Zhou and Han ancient coins, large and small have matches; Song's armillary instrument foot measure and measure have no error.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han coins confirm the measure; Song's armillary measure shows no error.

sentences.zh: 又依《淮南》，累粟十二成寸。

translations.literal: Also according to the Huainanzi, accumulating twelve millet grains makes one cun.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi also specifies twelve millet grains per cun.

sentences.zh: 明先王制法，索隱鉤深，以律計分，義無差異。

translations.literal: Showing ancient kings' law-making, probing hidden depths and reaching into the profound—calculating fen by pitch standards, meaning without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient law-making probed deeply—calculating fen from pitch standards without discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 《漢書· 食貨志》云：「黃金方寸，其重一斤。

translations.literal: Now if calculating by number—the jade sheng volume in jade measure 110 cun eight fen and a fraction odd; hu volume 1,108 fen five li seven hao three miao nine hu.
translations.idiomatic: By calculation: jade sheng volume 110.8+ jade-measure cun; hu volume 1,108.57+ cun.

sentences.zh: 又甄鸞《算術》云：「玉升一升，得官斗一升三合四勺。

translations.literal: Also Zhen Luan's Calculation Methods says: "Jade sheng one sheng obtains official dou one sheng three he four shao."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Luan records: one jade sheng equals one official dou three he four shao.

sentences.zh: 「此玉升大而官斗小也。

translations.literal: This jade sheng is large and official dou is small.
translations.idiomatic: The jade sheng is large; the official dou is small.

sentences.zh: 以數計之，甄鸞所據後周官斗，積玉尺九十七寸有奇，斛積九百七十七寸有奇。

translations.literal: Calculating by number—Zhen Luan's cited Northern Zhou official dou volume in jade measure 97 cun and a fraction odd; hu volume 977 cun and a fraction odd.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Luan's Northern Zhou official dou: 97+ jade-measure cun; hu 977+ cun.

sentences.zh: 後周玉鬥並副金錯銅斗及建德六年金錯題銅斗，實同以秬黍定量。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou jade dipper together with auxiliary gold-inlaid copper dou and Jiande sixth year gold-inlaid copper dou—in reality all the same, using black millet to fix capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou jade dipper, gold-inlaid copper dou, and Jiande 6 dou all used black millet for capacity.

sentences.zh: 以玉稱權之，一升之實，皆重六斤十三兩。

translations.literal: Weighing with jade steelyard—the solid content of one sheng all weighs six jin thirteen liang.
translations.idiomatic: Weighed on the jade steelyard, one sheng solid content weighed six jin thirteen liang.

sentences.zh: 開皇以古斗三升為一升。

translations.literal: Kaihuang used three ancient dou as one sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang used three ancient dou per sheng.

sentences.zh: 大業初，依復古鬥。

translations.literal: Daye beginning, following restored ancient dou.
translations.idiomatic: Daye initially restored the ancient dou.

sentences.zh: ○衡權衡者，平也；

translations.literal: ○ Steelyard and Weights. Steelyard means balance;
translations.idiomatic: ○ Steelyard and Weights. The steelyard denotes balance;

sentences.zh: 權者，重也。

translations.literal: weight means heaviness.
translations.idiomatic: while weight denotes heaviness.

sentences.zh: 衡所以任權而鈞物平輕重也。

translations.literal: The steelyard is what bears weights and balances things, leveling light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The steelyard bears weights and balances light and heavy.

sentences.zh: 其道如底，以見准之正，繩之直。

translations.literal: Its Way is like a base—to show the leveling's correctness, the cord's straightness.
translations.idiomatic: Its principle is like a base—showing the level's correctness and the cord's straightness.

sentences.zh: 左旋見規，右折見矩。

translations.literal: Turning left reveals the compass; turning right reveals the square.
translations.idiomatic: Turn left to reveal the compass; turn right the square.

sentences.zh: 其在天也，佐助璿璣，斟酌建指，以齊七政，故曰玉衡。

translations.literal: In Heaven it assists the armillary sphere, adjusting and establishing the pointer, to align the seven regulators—therefore called jade steelyard.
translations.idiomatic: In Heaven it assists the armillary sphere, adjusting the pointer to align the seven regulators—the jade steelyard.

sentences.zh: 權者，銖、兩、斤、鈞、石也，以秤物平施，知輕重也。

translations.literal: Weights are zhu, liang, jin, jun, and shi—using scales to balance things evenly, knowing light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Weights are zhu, liang, jin, jun, shi—using scales to know light and heavy.

sentences.zh: 古有黍、Ｒ、錘、錙、鐶、鉤、鋝、鎰之目，歷代差變，其詳未聞。

translations.literal: Antiquity had categories of millet, R, chui, zi, huan, gou, lue, and yi—the dynasties differed and changed; details are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity had millet, R, chui, zi, huan, gou, lue, and yi weight units—dynastic variations unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 《前志》曰：權本起于黃鐘之重。

translations.literal: The Former Treatise says: Weights originate from Yellow Bell's weight.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Treatise: weights originate from Yellow Bell's weight.

sentences.zh: 一龠容千二百黍，重十二銖。

translations.literal: One pitch key holds 1,200 millet grains, weighing twelve zhu.
translations.idiomatic: One pitch key holds 1,200 grains, weighing twelve zhu.

sentences.zh: 兩之為兩，二十四銖為兩。

translations.literal: Two make a liang; twenty-four zhu make a liang.
translations.idiomatic: Two keys make a liang; twenty-four zhu a liang.

sentences.zh: 十六兩為斤。

translations.literal: Sixteen liang make a jin.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen liang equal one jin.

sentences.zh: 三十斤為鈞。

translations.literal: Thirty jin make a jun.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty jin equal one jun.

sentences.zh: 四鈞為石。

translations.literal: Four jun make a shi.
translations.idiomatic: Four jun equal one shi.

sentences.zh: 五權謹矣。

translations.literal: The five weights are verified.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the five weight units are verified.

sentences.zh: 其制以義立之，以物鈞之。

translations.literal: Its system is established by principle, balanced by things.
translations.idiomatic: Established by principle, balanced by things.

sentences.zh: 其餘大小之差，以輕重為宜。

translations.literal: Other differences of large and small—according to light and heavy as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Other size differences follow light and heavy as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 圜而環之，令之肉倍好者，周旋亡端，終而複始，亡窮已也。

translations.literal: Round and looped—making the flesh double the hole—turning without end, finishing and beginning again, never exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Round and looped with flesh double the hole—turning endlessly, never exhausted.

sentences.zh: 權與物鈞而生衡，衡運生規，規圓生矩，矩方生繩，繩直生准。

translations.literal: Weights balance with things and generate the steelyard; steelyard movement generates the compass; compass roundness generates the square; square generates the cord; cord straightness generates the leveling base.
translations.idiomatic: Weights balance things and generate the steelyard; steelyard motion the compass; compass roundness the square; square the cord; cord the leveling base.

sentences.zh: 准正則衡平而鈞權矣。

translations.literal: Leveling base correct then steelyard balanced and weights equalized.
translations.idiomatic: Correct leveling base means balanced steelyard and equalized weights.

sentences.zh: 是為五則，備於鈞器，以為大範。

translations.literal: These are the five standards, complete in the steelyard instrument, as the great model.
translations.idiomatic: These five standards, complete in the steelyard, form the great model.

sentences.zh: 案《趙書》，石勒十八年七月，造建德殿，得圓石，狀如水碓。

translations.literal: Examining the Zhao History—in Shi Le's eighteenth year seventh month, building the Jiande Hall, a round stone was obtained, shaped like a water pestle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao History records: Shi Le's eighteenth year, seventh month, building Jiande Hall, a round stone like a water pestle was found.

sentences.zh: 其銘曰：「律權石，重四鈞，同律度量衡。

translations.literal: Its inscription says: "Pitch-standard weight shi, weight four jun, same pitch standard measure steelyard weights."
translations.idiomatic: Inscription: "Pitch-standard weight shi, four jun weight, unified pitch, measure, and steelyard."

sentences.zh: 有辛氏造。

translations.literal: Made by the Xin clan."
translations.idiomatic: It was made by the Xin clan."

sentences.zh: 」續咸議是王莽時物。

translations.literal: Xu Xian held this was a Wang Mang-era object.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xian identified it as Wang Mang-era.

sentences.zh: 後魏景明中，并州人王顯達獻古銅權一枚，上銘八十一字。

translations.literal: Later Wei Jingming era—a Bingzhou man Wang Xianda presented an ancient copper weight, upper inscription eighty-one characters.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Jingming—a Bingzhou man Wang Xianda presented an ancient copper weight with eighty-one-character inscription.

sentences.zh: 其銘云：律權石，重四鈞。

translations.literal: Its inscription says: Pitch-standard weight shi, weight four jun."
translations.idiomatic: Inscription: "Pitch-standard weight shi, four jun."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「黃帝初祖，德匝于虞。

translations.literal: Also says: "Yellow Emperor's first ancestor, virtue extending to Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Also: "Yellow Emperor's first ancestor, virtue extending to Yu."

sentences.zh: 虞帝始祖，德匝於新。

translations.literal: Yu Emperor's first ancestor, virtue extending to Xin."
translations.idiomatic: The Yu Emperor's first ancestor, whose virtue extended to Xin."

sentences.zh: 歲在大樑，龍集戊辰。

translations.literal: Year in Great Beam, dragon gathering wuchen."
translations.idiomatic: In the year Great Beam, the dragon gathered at wuchen."

sentences.zh: 戊辰直定，天命有人。

translations.literal: Wuchen directly fixed, Heaven's Mandate has a person."
translations.idiomatic: At wuchen directly fixed, Heaven's Mandate found its bearer."

sentences.zh: 據土德受，正號即真。

translations.literal: Receiving according to earth virtue, correct title then true."
translations.idiomatic: Receiving earth virtue, correct title then true."

sentences.zh: 改正建醜，長壽隆崇。

translations.literal: Correcting calendar establishing chou, long life lofty and grand."
translations.idiomatic: Correcting the calendar and establishing chou, long life lofty and grand."

sentences.zh: 同律度量衡，稽當前人。

translations.literal: Same pitch standard measure steelyard, examining and matching predecessors."
translations.idiomatic: Unified pitch, measure, and steelyard, examining predecessors."

sentences.zh: 龍在己巳，歲次實沈，初班天下，萬國永遵。

translations.literal: Dragon at jisi, year sequence Shi Shen, first promulgation throughout the realm, ten thousand states forever following."
translations.idiomatic: Dragon at jisi, year Shi Shen, first promulgated empire-wide, ten thousand states forever following."

sentences.zh: 子子孫孫，享傳億年。

translations.literal: Sons sons grandsons grandsons, enjoying transmission for a hundred million years."
translations.idiomatic: Sons and grandsons, enjoying transmission for a hundred million years."

sentences.zh: 」此亦王莽所制也。

translations.literal: This also was made by Wang Mang.
translations.idiomatic: This was also Wang Mang's work.

sentences.zh: 其時太樂令公孫崇依《漢志》先修稱尺，及見此權，以新稱稱之，重一百二十斤。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Music Director Gongsun Chong, according to the Han Treatise first repaired the steelyard foot measure; upon seeing this weight, using the new steelyard to weigh it—weight 120 jin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Music Director Gongsun Chong first repaired the steelyard measure per the Han Treatise; weighing this object on the new steelyard—it weighed 120 jin.

sentences.zh: 新稱與權，合若符契。

translations.literal: New steelyard and weight matched like tally and seal.
translations.idiomatic: The new steelyard and weight matched like seal and tally.

sentences.zh: 於是付崇調樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon entrusted to Chong to tune music.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was then charged with tuning music.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，一依《漢志》作鬥尺。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowen's time, dou and foot measure were made entirely according to the Han Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen, dou and foot measure were made per the Han Treatise.

sentences.zh: 梁、陳依古稱。

translations.literal: Liang and Chen followed the ancient steelyard.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Chen used the ancient steelyard.

sentences.zh: 齊以古稱一斤八兩為一斤。

translations.literal: Qi used ancient steelyard one jin eight liang as one jin.
translations.idiomatic: Qi counted eight ancient liang as one jin.

sentences.zh: 周玉稱四兩，當古稱四兩半。

translations.literal: Zhou jade steelyard four liang equals ancient steelyard four liang and a half.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou jade steelyard four liang equaled ancient steelyard four and a half liang.

sentences.zh: 開皇以古稱三斤為一斤，大業中，依復古秤。

translations.literal: Kaihuang used ancient steelyard three jin as one jin; in Daye, following restored ancient steelyard.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang counted three ancient jin as one jin; Daye restored the ancient steelyard.
